intro:
Swap USDC from Arbitrum One to ETH on Ethereum. Circle USDC leaves Arbitrum One and native ETH arrives on Ethereum.

The spend is Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. Open that contract on Arbiscan and confirm the wallet is on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Arbitrum Nova. Gas there is ETH, so a USDC balance alone cannot pay the fee. The receive marker is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the native gas sentinel. On Ethereum, chain id 1, that means ETH itself, not the WETH contract. Etherscan is the explorer for the arrival. Ethereum blocks are about 12 seconds, and that figure describes blocks, not when a bridge credits you.
description: Swap Circle USDC on Arbitrum One for native ETH on Ethereum. Match the Circle contract on Arbiscan and the gas sentinel on Etherscan before you sign it.

sections.heading: Circle USDC, not the bridged balance
sections.body: Circle issues 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbitrum One. It is six decimals. Many wallets still list an older bridged USDC.e row beside it. This quote spends the Circle contract only. If the coins sit in the bridged row, the amount you can sell here will look too small. Approving Circle USDC does not approve the other contract. Read the token address on the approval screen and match it to Arbiscan before you sign.

sections.heading: Native ETH is an account balance
sections.body: What arrives is ETH on Ethereum, the gas coin of chain id 1. The sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is how a quote names that balance. It is not a token contract with a supply page on Etherscan. You will not see an ERC-20 transfer for the received ETH. You should see the account balance change. If a dapp later asks for an ERC-20 called ETH, it usually wants WETH, and this page did not deliver that contract.

sections.heading: Two ETH balances that never merge
sections.body: The fee on Arbitrum One is also ETH, and that balance is not your Ethereum balance. Selling USDC does not refill the fee coin. Leave enough ETH on chain id 42161 for the approval and the swap. After ETH shows up on Ethereum you may still want a cushion there, because the next mainnet action spends some of what arrived. The guide on [how cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the right background if the two balances feel like one wallet.

sections.heading: Skip this page for WETH or a same-chain sell
sections.body: This route is wrong when the destination only accepts WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Native ETH will not pass an ERC-20 transfer check until you wrap it, and wrapping is a separate Ethereum transaction that needs gas. It is also the wrong page if you wanted Circle USDC to stay USDC on Ethereum, if you meant Arbitrum Nova, or if you only wanted to sell USDC for ETH inside Arbitrum One.

faqs.question: Is the ETH from this route the same token as WETH?
faqs.answer: No. WETH is the ERC-20 at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Ethereum. This route names native ETH with the gas sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. A contract that calls transfer on WETH will reject a plain ETH balance. Wrapping is a second step on chain id 1, and you should keep a little ETH so that wrap can pay its own fee.

faqs.question: I hold USDC.e on Arbitrum One. Will this spend it?
faqs.answer: No. This page spends Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. Bridged USDC.e is a different contract that older pools still use. If your balance sits there, the quote will look empty or short. Move those coins to native USDC first, or pick a route that names the bridged contract. Approving the Circle address does not unlock the bridged row.

faqs.question: Do I need ETH on Ethereum before I start?
faqs.answer: You need ETH on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, because that network charges gas in ETH. You do not need an existing ETH balance on Ethereum for the credit itself. The received asset is ETH. A follow-up transaction on mainnet also costs gas, so leave a little of the received ETH if you plan to move it again.

intro:
Swap USDC from Arbitrum One to WETH on Ethereum. Circle USDC leaves Arbitrum One and canonical WETH arrives on Ethereum.

The output contract is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. That is WETH on Ethereum, an ERC-20 you can open on Etherscan. It is not native ETH, and it is not the gas sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. The input is Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, which belongs on Arbiscan. Arbitrum One is chain id 42161, not Nova, and the fee is still ETH. Ethereum is chain id 1, with blocks about every 12 seconds. Those timings describe the chains, not a delivery schedule for WETH.
description: Swap Circle USDC on Arbitrum One for canonical WETH on Ethereum. Check both contracts on Arbiscan and Etherscan before you approve. Confirm the wallet network.

sections.heading: Pools that refuse the gas balance
sections.body: A lot of Ethereum liquidity is quoted against WETH, not against the raw account balance. Receiving 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 means the coins can sit in an ERC-20 pair without a separate wrap. If your only goal was gas for a mainnet transaction, this is an awkward shape, because WETH does not pay fees until you unwrap it. Unwrapping is another transaction on chain id 1, and it is not included here.

sections.heading: Match the full WETH address
sections.body: Etherscan should show the canonical WETH contract at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, not a lookalike that reused the ticker. Compare every character. On the spend side, Arbiscan should show Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. The symbol USDC is not enough, because bridged USDC.e still circulates on Arbitrum One and will not fund this quote.

sections.heading: Approval on Arbitrum, nothing similar for the receive
sections.body: Circle USDC is an ERC-20, so the wallet may ask for an approval before the swap can pull it. Set that approval on chain id 42161 and keep some ETH there for gas. You do not approve WETH in order to receive it. The receive is a credit on Ethereum. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) walks through why the approval belongs on the chain you are leaving.

sections.heading: Wrong page if you needed spendable gas
sections.body: Choose a different route if the wallet on Ethereum must hold native ETH at the sentinel address. WETH cannot cover gas until it is unwrapped, and the unwrap spends a bit of ETH you would not have yet if this were your first mainnet balance. This page is also wrong for Arbitrum Nova, for a same-chain USDC to ETH trade, and for anyone who wanted USDC to remain USDC on Ethereum.

faqs.question: Will this WETH pay gas on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on Ethereum is native ETH, the balance named by 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is an ERC-20. You can unwrap it later, but that transaction needs a little ETH already in the account. If you have no mainnet ETH at all, plan a route that delivers the gas coin instead of WETH.

faqs.question: Is Arbitrum WETH the token being sold?
faqs.answer: No. The sold token is Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. Arbitrum WETH, 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, is a different asset and will not be debited by this quote. If that wrapped balance is what you hold, open the WETH route. Approving USDC has no effect on WETH. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Does the 12 second Ethereum block set the wait?
faqs.answer: No. About 12 seconds is the typical Ethereum block interval you will see on Etherscan. Arbitrum One soft blocks are much faster, near a quarter of a second. Neither number is a promise for when WETH appears. If the quote expires before you sign, request a fresh one and read the minimum again.

intro:
Swap USDT from Arbitrum One to USDC on Ethereum. Tether USDT leaves Arbitrum One and Circle USDC arrives on Ethereum.

You are changing issuer as well as chain. The sold contract is Tether USDT at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbitrum One. Check it on Arbiscan. The bought contract is Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Ethereum. Check that one on Etherscan. Arbitrum One is chain id 42161, not Nova, and gas is ETH. Ethereum is chain id 1. Blocks there are about 12 seconds. That is not a clock for the issuer change.
description: Swap Tether USDT on Arbitrum One for Circle USDC on Ethereum. Compare both contracts on Arbiscan and Etherscan before signing. Match the receive address.

sections.heading: Two issuers, both six decimals
sections.body: Tether and Circle both use six decimals on these contracts, so the unit size looks familiar. The issuer does not. USDT at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 is Tether's token on Arbitrum One. USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 is Circle's token on Ethereum. A quote can show a small gap even when both aim at a dollar, because liquidity and fees sit between them. Read the minimum received instead of assuming one-for-one.

sections.heading: Where each explorer fits
sections.body: Arbiscan is only for the spend. If the USDT page you opened is on Etherscan, you are looking at Ethereum's Tether contract, 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, which this route does not sell. Etherscan is for the USDC you hope to receive. Chain id 42161 must be selected when you approve. Chain id 1 is where the Circle balance should appear. Mixing those explorers is how a pasted address goes to the wrong network.

sections.heading: ETH for the fee, dollars for the trade
sections.body: Neither stablecoin pays gas on Arbitrum One. Keep ETH in the same wallet on chain id 42161. The approval and the swap are separate costs if the allowance is short. You do not need USDC on Ethereum before the credit. You may want a little ETH on Ethereum later if you will move that USDC, because mainnet transfers are not free. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is the network that will hold the Circle balance.

sections.heading: Stay on this page only for an issuer switch
sections.body: This route is wrong if you wanted Tether USDT to remain Tether on Ethereum. It does not deliver 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. It is wrong if you wanted DAI from Maker, and wrong if the balance you hold is a bridged dollar rather than 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. It is also the wrong page for Arbitrum Nova or for a same-chain swap that never needed Ethereum.

faqs.question: Are these two contracts the same USDC?
faqs.answer: No. The token you sell is Tether USDT at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbitrum One. The token you can receive is Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Ethereum. Same six-decimal style, different companies. Confirm the receive address on Etherscan. A wallet label that only says USD is not a match.

faqs.question: Why might the dollar amount move?
faqs.answer: Both assets target a dollar, but the route still crosses liquidity. Fees and the book between Tether and Circle can leave you with a little less than the amount you typed. The number that matters is the minimum on the quote. If that minimum is below what you will accept, do not sign.

faqs.question: Can I receive this USDC on Arbitrum Nova?
faqs.answer: No. The spend network is Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, and the receive network is Ethereum, chain id 1. Nova is a different Arbitrum chain and will not show this Circle balance. If your wallet is pointed at Nova, switch to Arbitrum One before you approve USDT on Arbiscan's contract.

intro:
Swap USDT from Arbitrum One to DAI on Ethereum. Tether USDT is spent, and Maker DAI is what can arrive.

DAI on Ethereum is the Maker contract 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. It uses eighteen decimals, not six. Open it on Etherscan. The USDT you sell is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbitrum One, and Arbiscan is where that page lives. That USDT is Tether. Arbitrum One is chain id 42161, not Nova, and the fee is ETH. Ethereum is chain id 1. A block there is about 12 seconds. Do not treat that interval as a time for the credit to land.
description: Swap Tether USDT on Arbitrum One for Maker DAI on Ethereum. Match both contracts on Arbiscan and Etherscan, and mind the decimals. Leave source gas ready.

sections.heading: Maker issues DAI, Tether does not
sections.body: DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is Maker's stablecoin on Ethereum. It is backed by collateral inside Maker's system, not by Tether's reserves and not by Circle. The token leaving Arbitrum One is Tether USDT. A wallet that only checks the word dollar will hide that change of issuer. If your destination app whitelists Circle USDC only, DAI will not satisfy it, even though both are often called stablecoins.

sections.heading: Six decimals out, eighteen in
sections.body: Arbitrum USDT uses six decimals. Ethereum DAI uses eighteen. The raw integer on the receive side is much larger for the same dollar size, and a sloppy copy of the smallest unit will look absurd. Trust the human amount on the quote, then confirm the contract on Etherscan so you know the decimals belong to Maker DAI. Do not compare the raw unit of USDT with the raw unit of DAI and call the gap a fee.

sections.heading: ETH still pays the Arbitrum fee
sections.body: Selling USDT does not pay gas. Chain id 42161 charges ETH. Keep a fee balance beside the Tether balance. You are not asked to approve DAI in order to receive it. Approval, if the allowance is empty, is for 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbitrum One. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is worth reading if the approval chain and the receive chain feel swapped.

sections.heading: Use another route for Circle or for Tether
sections.body: This page is wrong if you wanted Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, and wrong if you wanted Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. It does not deliver either. It is wrong on Arbitrum Nova, wrong for a same-chain swap, and wrong if you think DAI is just USDT under another ticker. Native ETH, named by the 0xEeee sentinel, is also not what arrives.

faqs.question: Is DAI on this route issued by Tether or Circle?
faqs.answer: Neither. The DAI you can receive is Maker's contract at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Ethereum. Tether is the issuer of the USDT you spend, 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. Circle is not in this pair. Check the Maker address on Etherscan before you treat the balance as the dollar token a protocol expects.

faqs.question: Why does the unit size look different?
faqs.answer: USDT on Arbitrum One has six decimals. DAI on Ethereum has eighteen. One DAI is a much larger raw integer than one USDT. The quote should show both amounts in whole tokens. If you are comparing base units from the two explorers, the integers will not match even when the dollar value is close.

faqs.question: Does this page also unwrap ETH?
faqs.answer: No. ETH and WETH are not the assets in this quote. You spend Tether and you can receive Maker DAI. The gas sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is not the output. You still need a little ETH on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, to pay the fee. Nova is the wrong network for that fee.

intro:
Swap USDT from Arbitrum One to ETH on Ethereum. Tether USDT leaves Arbitrum One and native ETH arrives on Ethereum.

Tether's contract on the way out is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. Confirm it on Arbiscan while the wallet sits on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Nova. The way in is native ETH, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. That sentinel means the gas coin on Ethereum, chain id 1, not WETH. Etherscan will not show a token supply for it. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. The bridge does not inherit that tempo as a promised credit time.
description: Swap Tether USDT on Arbitrum One for native ETH on Ethereum. Verify USDT on Arbiscan and the gas sentinel on Etherscan. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: A dollar token in, a volatile coin out
sections.body: USDT is built to track a dollar. ETH is not. Between the quote and the signature, the ETH amount can move. The minimum received is the floor you accept. If that floor is no longer enough, wait for a new quote rather than signing a stale one. Nothing here locks the price of ETH while a message moves between Arbitrum One and Ethereum. Size the trade for a move you can tolerate.

sections.heading: The sentinel is not an ERC-20
sections.body: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE stands in for native gas. On this route the destination chain is Ethereum, so the credit is ETH in the account, not an ERC-20 transfer you can watch on a token page. Etherscan's transaction view for the destination wallet is the useful check. If someone sends you a token contract and calls it ETH, compare it with WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. That contract is a different asset.

sections.heading: Keep fee ETH even though you are selling USDT
sections.body: The asset you sell is Tether, but the fee on chain id 42161 is ETH. An empty ETH balance on Arbitrum One stops the approval and the swap. USDT cannot substitute. After native ETH arrives on Ethereum, that new balance is mainnet ETH, not a refund of the fee you already paid on Arbitrum. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) uses the same ticker for gas and still keeps a separate balance.

sections.heading: Not the page for staying in dollars
sections.body: Skip this route if you wanted Circle USDC or Maker DAI on Ethereum. Both would be stablecoin outcomes. This one is ETH. Skip it if you needed WETH specifically, if your USDT is not 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, or if the wallet is on Arbitrum Nova. A same-chain sale of USDT for ETH on Arbitrum One is also a different task, because nothing would arrive on Ethereum.

faqs.question: Does native ETH on Ethereum equal WETH?
faqs.answer: No. This route credits the gas balance, using the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. WETH is the separate contract 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Protocols that only pull WETH will not see your ETH until you wrap it. Wrapping on Ethereum costs a little of that ETH in gas, so do not plan to wrap the entire balance.

faqs.question: Which USDT contract does Arbiscan need to show?
faqs.answer: 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. That is Tether USDT on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Ethereum's Tether contract, 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, is not what you spend. If the wallet is on Nova, the Arbiscan contract for One will not match the network, and the approval will be on the wrong chain.

faqs.question: Will the ETH amount stay fixed while I review?
faqs.answer: Only until the quote expires. ETH is volatile against USDT, so a pause can change the minimum. Read the floor again before you sign. About 12 seconds on Etherscan is an Ethereum block interval, not a guarantee that the same ETH amount is still available. If the quote lapses, request another and check the new minimum.

intro:
Swap USDT from Arbitrum One to WETH on Ethereum. Tether USDT leaves Arbitrum One and WETH arrives here on Ethereum.

WETH here is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, the canonical contract on Ethereum. Read it on Etherscan. It is an ERC-20, not the native gas sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. The sold asset is Tether USDT at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, which you confirm on Arbiscan. Source chain id is 42161, Arbitrum One, not Nova. Fee token is ETH. Destination chain id is 1. Ethereum blocks average about 12 seconds and do not schedule the bridge.
description: Swap Tether USDT on Arbitrum One for canonical WETH on Ethereum. Check Arbiscan for USDT and Etherscan for the WETH contract. Confirm the wallet network.

sections.heading: WETH9 is the contract you should see
sections.body: The address 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is the usual WETH9 deployment on Ethereum. Other contracts have used the same ticker. Etherscan's token page for that exact address is the one that counts. If a portfolio labels a different contract as WETH, do not treat it as the output of this quote. The input side is stricter too: only Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbitrum One is the spend.

sections.heading: Receiving WETH does not fill the gas tank
sections.body: You can hold a large WETH balance on Ethereum and still be unable to send a transaction, because fees come from native ETH. If this wallet has never held mainnet ETH, plan for that gap before you rely on the WETH. Unwrapping WETH into ETH is possible later, but the unwrap itself needs gas you do not get from this route. The sentinel address is what a gas-seeking route would have used instead.

sections.heading: Approve Tether, not the destination
sections.body: If USDT allowance is zero, the wallet asks for approval on Arbitrum One before it can move 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. Pay that approval in ETH. You do not approve the Ethereum WETH contract to receive it. A receiver address has to be a normal Ethereum account that can hold ERC-20s. The steps in [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) keep the approval on the source network.

sections.heading: Switch routes for native ETH or for DAI
sections.body: This is the wrong page if you need native ETH on Ethereum to pay gas immediately. It is the wrong page if you wanted Maker DAI or Circle USDC. It is the wrong page if you meant to sell Arbitrum WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 rather than Tether. Nova, and a swap that should stay inside Arbitrum One, are different jobs as well.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap this WETH without already having ETH?
faqs.answer: Unwrapping calls the WETH contract and the call needs gas. Gas is native ETH, not WETH. If the Ethereum account has no ETH, the unwrap cannot be submitted. This route delivers 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 only. Use a route that credits the 0xEeee sentinel if the next thing you must do is pay a mainnet fee.

faqs.question: Is Arbitrum USDT the same contract as Ethereum USDT?
faqs.answer: No. You spend 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, Tether on Arbitrum One. Ethereum Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, and this quote does not sell it or deliver it. Check the spend on Arbiscan under chain id 42161. The WETH you can receive is only on Ethereum, chain id 1. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Does WETH on Ethereum track native ETH one for one?
faqs.answer: The canonical WETH contract is designed so one WETH redeems for one ETH, minus the gas of the unwrap. That relationship is not the same thing as holding ETH already. This quote is also a market from USDT into WETH, so the amount of WETH depends on price and fees. Read the minimum.

intro:
Swap ETH from Arbitrum One to USDC on Ethereum. Native ETH leaves Arbitrum One and Circle USDC arrives on Ethereum.

The asset you spend is native ETH on Arbitrum One, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. That sentinel means the gas coin, not WETH. The same balance also pays the fee, so the quote cannot use every wei. What you can receive is Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Confirm it on Etherscan. Arbitrum One is chain id 42161, not Nova. Look at the spend on Arbiscan. Ethereum is chain id 1, and a block there is about 12 seconds, which is not a bridge timer.
description: Swap native ETH on Arbitrum One for Circle USDC on Ethereum. Keep fee ETH back, and match the USDC contract on Etherscan. Review the minimum received.

sections.heading: The gas coin is the asset you are selling
sections.body: On this route the thing you sell and the thing that pays the fee are the same native ETH balance on chain id 42161. If you type your full balance, the transaction has nothing left for gas and the wallet should refuse it. Leave a cushion. WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is not this balance. If the portfolio shows wrapped ether only, this quote is looking at the wrong row and will not see those coins.

sections.heading: Circle USDC on mainnet is six decimals
sections.body: 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 is Circle's USDC on Ethereum. Six decimals, fiat-backed by Circle, not Maker DAI and not Tether. Etherscan is the check. There is no USDC.e story on Ethereum mainnet the way there is on Arbitrum. Still compare the full address, because a token can print the letters USDC without being Circle. The receive account must be able to hold ERC-20s on chain id 1.

sections.heading: You do not bridge the ETH ticker through
sections.body: Native ETH on Arbitrum One is not delivered as native ETH on Ethereum by this page. The output is a dollar token. Your Arbitrum ETH balance falls. An Ethereum USDC balance can rise. They are different assets on different chain ids. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) covers why a shared ticker does not mean a shared balance, which matters here because both networks use ETH for gas.

sections.heading: Wrong when you wanted ETH to stay ETH
sections.body: Pick another page if the goal is WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, or if you wanted native ETH on Ethereum at the sentinel. This output is Circle USDC only. It is also the wrong page if you are holding WETH rather than gas ETH, if the wallet is on Nova, or if you only needed USDC inside Arbitrum One and had no reason to touch Ethereum.

faqs.question: Why can't I enter my entire ETH balance?
faqs.answer: Because 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Arbitrum One is both the asset sold and the fee coin. The swap and any approval-like costs still need ETH left in the account. Spend less than the full balance. WETH is a separate contract, 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, and is not a backup for this fee.

faqs.question: Is the USDC I receive Circle's contract?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the receive address is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Ethereum. That is Circle USDC, six decimals. Confirm it on Etherscan, chain id 1. Tether's USDT and Maker's DAI are different contracts. If a dapp asks for one of those, this route has delivered the wrong stablecoin for that dapp.

faqs.question: Does Arbitrum Nova use this same ETH balance?
faqs.answer: No. Nova is not chain id 42161. ETH on Arbitrum One does not sit on Nova, and it does not sit on Ethereum either. This page starts on Arbitrum One and can credit Circle USDC on Ethereum. If the wallet header says Nova, change the network before you sign. Arbiscan for One will not match a Nova transaction.

intro:
Swap ETH from Arbitrum One to USDT on Ethereum. Native ETH leaves Arbitrum One and Tether USDT arrives on Ethereum.

Spend the gas sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. That is native ETH, not WETH, and Arbiscan is the explorer for the network you are leaving. Keep some of that ETH for the fee. The contract you can receive is Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Ethereum. Open it on Etherscan. Chain id 1 produces blocks about every 12 seconds. That cadence is not a promise about USDT showing up.
description: Swap native ETH on Arbitrum One for Tether USDT on Ethereum. Reserve gas, and confirm 0xdAC17 on Etherscan before you sign. Review the minimum received.

sections.heading: Ethereum Tether is a fussy contract
sections.body: 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is the long-standing Tether deployment on Ethereum, six decimals. It does not behave like a textbook ERC-20 in every wallet because its approve function does not return a boolean. Receiving it is still a normal credit. Trouble shows up later, when you try to spend that USDT and a wallet misreads the approval. If a later spend looks stuck, check the allowance on Etherscan before you blame the bridge.

sections.heading: Leave gas behind on Arbitrum One
sections.body: You are selling native ETH, which is also the fee token on chain id 42161. The full balance is not available to the quote. WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 will not be touched, and it will not pay the fee either. Nova uses a different chain id. If the wallet is pointed there, you are not on the network this route debits, no matter what the ETH ticker says.

sections.heading: Price can move while the quote sits
sections.body: ETH against USDT is a market, not a fixed redemption. The minimum on the quote is your bound. When the quote goes stale, the bound goes with it. Request a new quote and read the new USDT floor. Tether aims at a dollar. ETH does not. A quiet hour and a violent hour are different trades even when the contract addresses stay the same. Do not sign a minimum you have not reread.

sections.heading: Not Circle, not DAI, not wrapped ether
sections.body: This page is wrong if you wanted Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 or Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. It is wrong if you wanted WETH on Ethereum, and wrong if you wanted to keep native ETH and only move chains. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) will show Tether, not a gas balance, as the asset this quote can add.

faqs.question: Which USDT address should Etherscan show?
faqs.answer: 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. That is Tether on Ethereum, six decimals. Arbitrum Tether, 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, is a different contract and is not the receive asset here. You are spending native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on Arbitrum One. Match both sides before you approve anything later. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Why might a later USDT approval look odd?
faqs.answer: The Ethereum USDT contract's approve call does not return a boolean the way many ERC-20s do. Some wallets show a warning even when the allowance was set. Check the allowance on Etherscan for 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 before you send a second approval. Receiving USDT on this route does not itself require that approval.

faqs.question: Is this the same as wrapping ETH on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: No. Wrapping locally would mint WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 and you would stay on Arbitrum One. This route sells native ETH and can credit Tether USDT on Ethereum, chain id 1. If you wanted WETH on Ethereum, this is the wrong output. Keep fee ETH on chain id 42161 so the sell can be signed.

intro:
Swap ETH from Arbitrum One to DAI on Ethereum. Native ETH leaves Arbitrum One and Maker DAI arrives on Ethereum.

You spend the native gas balance on Arbitrum One, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, chain id 42161, not Nova. Arbiscan is the explorer for that side. Do not spend the last wei, because ETH also pays the fee. Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is what Etherscan should show on the way in. That contract is eighteen decimals on Ethereum, chain id 1. Blocks there are about 12 seconds. The interval is a property of Ethereum, not a delivery promise.
description: Swap native ETH on Arbitrum One for Maker DAI on Ethereum. Reserve fee ETH and confirm the Maker contract on Etherscan. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: DAI is Maker's collateral stablecoin
sections.body: 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is issued through Maker, not through Circle and not through Tether. It does not become USDC because a wallet groups stablecoins together. Eighteen decimals means the base unit is tiny compared with six-decimal USDC or USDT. Read the DAI amount on the quote in whole tokens. If a lending market only accepts Circle's contract, this arrival will not be eligible collateral there.

sections.heading: Selling gas means reserving gas
sections.body: The sentinel names native ETH, which is the fee coin on Arbitrum One. A quote for the entire balance cannot pay for itself. Leave a remainder. The WETH contract 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is a different row. Selling wrapped ether is a different route. If you unwrap WETH first so you can use this page, that unwrap is its own transaction and also costs ETH.

sections.heading: What changes in the two portfolios
sections.body: Arbitrum One loses native ETH. Ethereum can gain DAI. You do not gain ETH on chain id 1, so you do not suddenly have mainnet gas. If you will move the DAI after it appears, you need ETH on Ethereum from somewhere else to pay that later fee. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is a useful companion when the receive asset cannot pay the next transaction.

sections.heading: Wrong output if you wanted a fiat stablecoin
sections.body: Leave this page if the destination whitelist says Circle USDC or Tether USDT. Maker DAI will not match those addresses. Leave it if you wanted WETH or native ETH on Ethereum. Leave it if the wallet is on Arbitrum Nova, or if the ETH you hold is already wrapped. A local wrap on Arbitrum One never reaches the Maker contract on Etherscan.

faqs.question: Is DAI the same as USDC with another name?
faqs.answer: No. Circle USDC on Ethereum is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This route can credit Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Different issuer, different decimals, different contract. Confirm the page on Etherscan. If your app's allowlist names Circle, do not send this route and hope the ticker is close enough. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Will I have ETH for gas on Ethereum afterward?
faqs.answer: Not from this quote. You sold native ETH on Arbitrum One and the output is DAI. Chain id 1 still charges ETH for transactions. Receiving DAI does not create that gas balance. If the Ethereum wallet is empty of ETH, you can hold DAI and still be unable to transfer it until some ETH arrives by another path.

faqs.question: What if my Arbitrum balance is WETH, not ETH?
faqs.answer: Then this page is the wrong one. It spends the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which is native ETH. Wrapped ether lives at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Unwrap first if you truly want this route, and keep enough ETH for the unwrap and the swap. Arbitrum Nova is not a substitute network.

intro:
Swap ETH from Arbitrum One to WETH on Ethereum. Native ETH leaves Arbitrum One and canonical WETH arrives on Ethereum.

This is not the wrap button inside one network. You spend native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Arbiscan is the explorer, and the network is not Nova. You can receive WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Ethereum. That contract is what Etherscan should show. It is not the Ethereum gas sentinel. Chain id 1 blocks are about 12 seconds. Wrapping locally would never produce that mainnet address.
description: Swap native ETH on Arbitrum One for canonical WETH on Ethereum. This is not a same-chain wrap. Confirm both on the explorers. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: A local wrap stops on Arbitrum
sections.body: If you wrap ETH on Arbitrum One, you mint 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 and the coins stay on chain id 42161. This page does something else. It takes native ETH on Arbitrum One and can credit the Ethereum WETH contract 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Same idea of wrapped ether, two different deployments, two chain ids. Do not paste the Arbitrum WETH address into an Ethereum field and expect a match.

sections.heading: Reserve fee ETH before you set the amount
sections.body: Native ETH pays the Arbitrum fee and is also the sold asset. The quote has to leave a remainder. If you unwrap nothing and simply spend the gas balance, watch the wallet's max button. It may offer a figure that fails once gas is added. WETH you already hold on Arbitrum is not spent here. Nova is not the fee network, even if the account dropdown looks similar.

sections.heading: Mainnet WETH still cannot pay mainnet gas
sections.body: Arriving WETH does not give you a native ETH balance on Ethereum. Fees on chain id 1 come from the sentinel balance. If you later unwrap 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, that call needs ETH already present. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where the wrapped contract lives. Read the minimum WETH on the quote, because ETH's price against the route can move before you sign.

sections.heading: Wrong if you wanted the gas coin on mainnet
sections.body: Choose a different output if the Ethereum wallet must pay gas right away. WETH is not that balance. This page is also wrong if you only needed to wrap inside Arbitrum One, if you wanted Circle USDC or Tether, or if the coins you hold are already WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Those wrapped coins need the WETH routes, not this native ETH route.

faqs.question: Is this just wrapping ETH on Arbitrum One?
faqs.answer: No. A wrap on Arbitrum One credits 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 and you remain on chain id 42161. This route spends native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and can credit Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Check that address on Etherscan. Arbiscan is only the source side. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Will the received WETH pay Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is native ETH. WETH is an ERC-20. The sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Ethereum is the balance that pays fees, and this route does not credit it. Unwrapping later needs some ETH in the account already. If you have none, pick a route that delivers native ETH instead of WETH.

faqs.question: Why leave some ETH unsold on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: The sold asset and the fee asset are the same native balance on chain id 42161. Selling the last wei leaves nothing for gas, so the signature cannot be submitted. Leave a cushion. Arbitrum Nova is a different chain and its ETH will not pay this route. Soft blocks near a quarter second are not a bridge schedule.

intro:
Swap WETH from Arbitrum One to USDC on Ethereum. Arbitrum WETH leaves the wallet and Circle USDC arrives on Ethereum.

The spend contract is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. That is WETH on Arbitrum One, an ERC-20, not the gas sentinel. Confirm it on Arbiscan. Chain id 42161, not Nova. You still need native ETH, 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, to pay the fee. Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 is the receive contract on Ethereum. Etherscan should show that address. Chain id 1, blocks about every 12 seconds, which does not time the credit.
description: Swap Arbitrum WETH for Circle USDC on Ethereum. The spend is 0x82aF, not native ETH. Confirm USDC on Etherscan. Leave ETH for the Arbitrum fee as well.

sections.heading: WETH and the gas row are neighbors, not twins
sections.body: A wallet can show ETH and WETH one line apart. This quote debits only 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Native ETH stays put except for the fee. If you meant to sell the gas balance, you are on the wrong page and the amount will not match what you see. If you hold WETH and the quote looks empty, the wallet is probably sitting on Nova or on a different WETH address than Arbiscan lists for One.

sections.heading: Approval is for the wrapped contract
sections.body: Because WETH is an ERC-20, the route may ask you to approve 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 before it can move. That approval is paid in native ETH on chain id 42161. You do not approve Circle USDC to receive it. Limit the allowance to what you intend to sell if the wallet lets you. An unlimited approval of WETH is a stronger permission than this one trade requires.

sections.heading: Circle on mainnet, six decimals
sections.body: The output is Circle's USDC, 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, not Tether and not Maker DAI. It is also not Ethereum WETH. You are leaving an ETH-linked token and arriving in a dollar token, so the minimum on the quote is a price, not a wrap ratio. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) helps if you expected one WETH to become one unit of something with the same ticker.

sections.heading: Skip it if the balance is still unwrapped
sections.body: This route is wrong when the coins are native ETH and you have not wrapped them. It is wrong when you wanted Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 rather than USDC. It is wrong for Nova, and wrong if you wanted USDC to stay on Arbitrum One. Unwrapping WETH locally and then selling ETH is a different sequence with an extra fee.

faqs.question: Does this route spend my Arbitrum ETH balance?
faqs.answer: Only the fee. The trade size comes from WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Native ETH is the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and is not the sold token. If that gas row is what you meant to sell, switch routes. Keep enough ETH on chain id 42161 so the WETH approval and the swap can both be signed.

faqs.question: Which USDC should appear on Etherscan?
faqs.answer: Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Ethereum, chain id 1. It has six decimals. Arbitrum Circle USDC, 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, is the source-chain token and is not what this route delivers. If you wanted that Arbitrum USDC, you are looking at a same-chain trade, not this bridge. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: What if I wanted WETH on Ethereum instead?
faqs.answer: Then this page is wrong. It can credit Circle USDC, not 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Selling Arbitrum WETH into mainnet WETH is a different output. Read the receive address on the quote and compare it with Etherscan. A ticker of ETH or WETH on the destination is not implied by the fact that you started with WETH.

intro:
Swap WETH from Arbitrum One to USDT on Ethereum. Arbitrum WETH leaves the wallet and Tether USDT arrives on Ethereum.

Sell 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, WETH on Arbitrum One. Arbiscan should show that contract, and the wallet should be on chain id 42161, not Nova. Native ETH at the 0xEeee sentinel pays the fee and is not the sold asset. Tether on the receive side is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Confirm it on Etherscan, chain id 1. Ethereum blocks are about 12 seconds. That is not how long the route takes.
description: Swap Arbitrum WETH for Tether USDT on Ethereum. Spend 0x82aF, receive 0xdAC17, and check both explorers before you sign. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: Tether on mainnet has history in the approve call
sections.body: The receive contract 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is Ethereum USDT, six decimals, issued by Tether. You do not approve it to receive it. When you later spend it, some wallets complain because approve does not return a boolean. Look at the allowance on Etherscan if a follow-up looks frozen. That quirk belongs to the token, not to the question of whether the bridge credit happened.

sections.heading: The wrapped balance needs its own allowance
sections.body: WETH will not move until 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 has allowance for the route, unless you already granted it. Native ETH cannot be approved in that ERC-20 sense, and this page is not asking it to be sold. If the allowance screen shows the sentinel address, you have selected the gas coin by mistake. Switch back to the WETH contract before you sign the permission.

sections.heading: Dollar output, ether input
sections.body: WETH tracks ETH inside its own contract, but the trade into USDT is still a sale of ether exposure. The minimum USDT can change while you read. Refresh the quote if you step away. Fees on Arbitrum One stay in ETH, so a wallet with WETH and zero ETH cannot finish. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) is the network that must hold both rows: wrapped coins to sell, and a little gas.

sections.heading: Not the route for Circle or for mainnet WETH
sections.body: This page does not deliver Circle USDC, Maker DAI, or Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. It does not deliver native ETH on Ethereum. It is the wrong page if your balance is unwrapped ETH, if you are on Nova, or if you wanted Arbitrum Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 to stay on Arbitrum One.

faqs.question: Is the USDT I receive the Arbitrum Tether contract?
faqs.answer: No. Arbitrum Tether is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. This route can credit Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Check that page on Etherscan. You spend WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. The two USDT deployments are not interchangeable. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Why is native ETH still required?
faqs.answer: Gas on Arbitrum One is native ETH, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. WETH is the asset being sold, not the fee token. Without a little ETH, the approval of 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 cannot be mined. USDT on Ethereum will not refund that fee. Nova ETH is not the fee balance for chain id 42161.

faqs.question: Can I treat the WETH amount as a fixed USDT amount?
faqs.answer: No. The route sells wrapped ether for Tether, and the price moves. Use the minimum on the quote as the floor. If the quote expires, that floor expires with it. Six decimals on Ethereum USDT do not change the need to reread the amount. About 12 seconds is an Ethereum block interval, not a price lock.

intro:
Swap WETH from Arbitrum One to DAI on Ethereum. Arbitrum WETH leaves the wallet and Maker DAI arrives on Ethereum.

Spend WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. That contract is on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, and Arbiscan is the place to read it. It is not native ETH. The fee still uses the gas sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is the receive contract, eighteen decimals, on Ethereum. Etherscan is the check. Chain id 1, blocks about every 12 seconds. None of that sets a bridge deadline.
description: Swap Arbitrum WETH for Maker DAI on Ethereum. Confirm 0x82aF on Arbiscan and the Maker contract on Etherscan first. Confirm both addresses on the explorers.

sections.heading: Eighteen decimal DAI against wrapped ether
sections.body: WETH uses eighteen decimals, and so does Maker DAI, but that coincidence is not a one-for-one redeem. You are selling ether exposure for a stablecoin. The amounts can look numerically close only when ETH's price is near a round dollar figure, and they will not stay lined up. Read DAI on the quote. Confirm 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan so you know you are counting Maker units, not a six-decimal stablecoin.

sections.heading: Issuer check before the wallet label
sections.body: Maker issues this DAI. Circle does not. Tether does not. A portfolio group called stables can hide the issuer. If the app you are funding lists Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, stop. This route will not produce that contract. The same is true for Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. The label DAI has to match the Maker address, not a bridged imitation on another chain.

sections.heading: Allowance sits on Arbitrum WETH
sections.body: Approve 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on chain id 42161 if the allowance is empty. Pay the approval in native ETH. Do not approve DAI. Do not approve WETH on Ethereum, because you are not spending that contract. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) puts the permission on the chain you leave, which is the pattern here.

sections.heading: Wrong for a plain unwrap or a USDC payout
sections.body: Unwrapping WETH on Arbitrum One would return native ETH on chain id 42161 and stop there. This page does not do that. It also does not pay native ETH or WETH on Ethereum. If your goal is Circle USDC, Tether, or a gas balance on mainnet, pick another route. If the wallet is on Nova, the WETH contract on Arbiscan for One is not the balance you are viewing.

faqs.question: Who issues the DAI this route can deliver?
faqs.answer: Maker. The contract is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Ethereum, and Etherscan is where you confirm it. It is not Circle USDC and it is not Tether USDT. You spend Arbitrum WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. If a protocol's allowlist names a different stablecoin, this arrival will not qualify. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Do equal decimals mean one WETH becomes one DAI?
faqs.answer: No. Both tokens use eighteen decimals, so the base units look similar in size. The trade is still a sale of wrapped ether for DAI at the quoted price, minus fees. One WETH is not redeemable for one DAI inside Maker by using this page. Read the minimum DAI. Refresh the quote if it expires.

faqs.question: Is the gas sentinel the token being sold?
faqs.answer: No. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is native ETH, used here only as gas on Arbitrum One. The sold contract is WETH, 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Chain id 42161 must be selected, not Nova. If you hold only unwrapped ETH, this quote cannot see a WETH balance to sell. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

intro:
Swap WETH from Arbitrum One to ETH on Ethereum. Arbitrum WETH leaves the wallet and native ETH arrives on Ethereum.

You sell the ERC-20 at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, not the gas coin. Check that WETH on Arbiscan. Arbitrum One is chain id 42161, not Nova. You still pay the fee in native ETH. The output marker is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which on Ethereum means the real gas balance, not WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Etherscan shows the account, not a token supply, for that sentinel. Chain id 1 blocks take about 12 seconds and do not clock the bridge.
description: Swap Arbitrum WETH for native ETH on Ethereum. Output is the gas sentinel, not mainnet WETH. Confirm it on Etherscan. Confirm both addresses on the explorers.

sections.heading: Unwrap on Arbitrum would never reach mainnet
sections.body: Calling withdraw on 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 returns native ETH on Arbitrum One. You stay on chain id 42161. This route is for people who want the gas coin on Ethereum instead. The receive marker is the same sentinel text, 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, but the chain id is 1, so the balance that can rise is mainnet ETH. Context is the chain, not the hex alone.

sections.heading: Why the fee and the sale are different rows
sections.body: You need native ETH on Arbitrum One to pay gas even though you are selling WETH. If you unwrapped everything already, you no longer hold the contract this page spends. If you have not unwrapped, you need a leftover gas balance beside the WETH. Emptying the gas row to zero, then trying to approve WETH, fails. Nova's ETH does not fill this gap on chain id 42161.

sections.heading: What a successful credit looks like
sections.body: You should not be hunting an ERC-20 transfer for the received ETH. The Ethereum account balance changes. Etherscan's internal transactions or the balance delta are the clues, depending on how the route delivers. You will not receive 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. If a dapp wanted that WETH, you would still have to wrap on mainnet, and wrapping spends a slice of the ETH you just received as gas.

sections.heading: Wrong page for wrapped output or for USDC
sections.body: Stay off this route if the destination contract must be WETH, Circle USDC, Tether, or Maker DAI. The output is native ETH only. Stay off it if you merely wanted to unwrap inside Arbitrum One. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the background for why unwrapping and bridging are separate jobs even when both end with something called ETH.

faqs.question: Does this deliver Ethereum WETH or native ETH?
faqs.answer: Native ETH. The output marker is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 1. Canonical WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and is not the credit. You spend Arbitrum WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. If a pool only accepts the WETH contract, wrap after arrival and keep gas for that wrap. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap WETH on Arbitrum and call it done?
faqs.answer: Only if you wanted ETH on Arbitrum One. Withdraw on 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 pays native ETH on chain id 42161. It does not create a balance on Ethereum. This page is the one that can credit mainnet ETH. Check the network in the wallet before you decide which action you are signing.

faqs.question: Why does the sentinel appear on both sides?
faqs.answer: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is a marker for native gas, not a unique token. On Arbitrum One it means the ETH you use for fees. On Ethereum it means the ETH you can receive. The sold token is still the WETH contract on Arbiscan. Read the chain id beside the marker. Nova is neither of these two networks.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to USDC on Ethereum. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and Circle USDC arrives here on Ethereum.

ARB is the governance token at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. It is not ETH and it does not pay gas. Confirm the contract on Arbiscan. The network is Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Nova. Fees are native ETH at the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Circle USDC you can receive is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Ethereum. Etherscan is the check. Chain id 1 blocks are about 12 seconds, which is not a credit schedule.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for Circle USDC on Ethereum. ARB is not gas. Confirm both contracts on Arbiscan and Etherscan. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: You are selling the governance token
sections.body: 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is ARB on Arbitrum One. Spending it means those units no longer vote from this wallet. The route does not escrow them for later voting, and it does not deliver ARB on Ethereum. The output is Circle USDC. If you still need ARB for a governance proposal, sell only the surplus. Eighteen decimals on ARB are not the six decimals you will see on the USDC side.

sections.heading: Gas is a second balance you must hold
sections.body: A wallet full of ARB and empty of ETH cannot approve or swap. Native ETH on chain id 42161 pays the fee. The sentinel is not ARB. Bridged representations and the official ARB contract are easy to confuse if you only read the ticker. Arbiscan's page for 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is the spend. Nova will not show this as the same chain even when the token name looks familiar.

sections.heading: Circle USDC is a price, not a peg to ARB
sections.body: ARB floats. USDC targets a dollar. The minimum on the quote is the only floor you have, and it expires with the quote. Do not treat a round number of ARB as a round number of dollars. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) explains the wait between networks, but it will not freeze the ARB price while you read. Refresh if you leave the screen.

sections.heading: Wrong if you wanted ARB to arrive as ARB
sections.body: This page is the wrong one when the goal is to hold ARB on Ethereum, or to hold ARB anywhere. It converts to Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. It is wrong for Tether, Maker DAI, WETH, and native ETH on mainnet. It is wrong if you meant a same-chain sale into USDC on Arbitrum One, where the Circle contract would be 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 instead.

faqs.question: Will I receive ARB on Ethereum from this page?
faqs.answer: No. You spend ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One, and the asset that can arrive is Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Confirm that USDC on Etherscan. If you need the governance token itself on another chain, this output is the wrong shape. You also give up the ARB you sell.

faqs.question: Does ARB pay the fee on Arbitrum One?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on chain id 42161. ARB is an ERC-20 and may need an approval, which also costs ETH. Arbitrum Nova is not this network. If the ETH row is empty, the ARB balance cannot move, no matter how large it is.

faqs.question: Is this USDC the same contract I use on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: No. Arbitrum Circle USDC is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. This route can credit Ethereum Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Both are Circle and both use six decimals, but they are different deployments. Check Etherscan for the receive address before you tell another app which USDC you hold. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to USDT on Ethereum. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and Tether USDT arrives here on Ethereum.

The governance token you sell is 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Read it on Arbiscan. Chain id 42161, Arbitrum One, not Nova. It is not the gas coin. Keep native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, for the fee. Tether you can receive is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Ethereum. That is the contract to open on Etherscan. Chain id 1, about 12 seconds per block, and that block time is not a fill promise.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for Tether USDT on Ethereum. Receive 0xdAC17, not ARB. Check Arbiscan and Etherscan before signing. Confirm the wallet network.

sections.heading: Ethereum USDT, including its approve quirk
sections.body: 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is Tether on Ethereum, six decimals. Receiving it does not require you to approve it. Spending it later might. That contract's approve function omits the boolean return some wallets expect, so a follow-up approval can throw a confusing warning. Verify allowance on Etherscan before repeating it. None of that changes the identity of the token: it is Tether, not Circle, and not the ARB you sold.

sections.heading: ARB allowance is the permission that matters
sections.body: If the route has no allowance on 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548, the wallet will ask for one on chain id 42161. Pay it in ETH. Do not grant that permission from a Nova session. Do not confuse ARB with Arbitrum WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. The tickers are unrelated. A governance balance and a wrapped ether balance can sit in the same wallet and only one of them funds this quote.

sections.heading: The dollar amount is a market
sections.body: ARB does not redeem at a fixed USDT rate. Liquidity, fees, and price all sit in the minimum. When the quote expires, so does the number. Tether can trade a hair away from one dollar as well, so two moving pieces are possible. Read the USDT floor in whole tokens, remembering six decimals, and ignore raw integer comparisons with eighteen-decimal ARB. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where that Tether balance would live.

sections.heading: Not a bridge of the ARB token itself
sections.body: If the plan is to hold ARB on Ethereum, this route is wrong because the output is USDT. If the plan is Circle USDC or Maker DAI, it is also wrong. If the plan is native ETH or WETH on mainnet, it is wrong. If you only wanted USDT on Arbitrum One, the local Tether contract is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 and this page is aimed at a different chain.

faqs.question: Does this route move ARB to Ethereum unchanged?
faqs.answer: No. ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is what you sell on Arbitrum One. The asset that can arrive is Tether USDT at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Ethereum. You will not see an ARB balance on Etherscan from this quote. If governance on the destination was the goal, stop and pick a different output.

faqs.question: Why might a future USDT approval warn me?
faqs.answer: Ethereum USDT at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 does not return a boolean from approve. Wallets sometimes flag that call even when the allowance updated. Read the allowance on Etherscan before you fire a second approval. This route's receive step does not need that approval. The approval you may sign now is for ARB on Arbitrum One.

faqs.question: What pays gas if I hold only ARB?
faqs.answer: Nothing on this route. Gas is native ETH on chain id 42161, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. ARB cannot substitute. Add ETH on Arbitrum One before you approve 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Arbitrum Nova is the wrong chain id for that ETH. The fee is not refunded as USDT. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to DAI on Ethereum. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and Maker DAI arrives here on Ethereum.

Sell governance token 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One. Arbiscan is the explorer, chain id 42161, not Nova. ARB does not pay fees. Native ETH uses the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE for gas. Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is the receive contract on Ethereum, eighteen decimals. Open it on Etherscan. Chain id 1, blocks about every 12 seconds. That rhythm is not a promise for DAI.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for Maker DAI on Ethereum. Output is 0x6B1754, not ARB. Match it on Etherscan before you sign. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: Both tokens are eighteen decimals, neither is a peg
sections.body: ARB and DAI both use eighteen decimals, so a careless glance at base units looks tidy. The economics are not tidy. ARB is a governance float. DAI is Maker's stablecoin. One ARB does not redeem for one DAI. The quote's minimum is the comparison that matters. Confirm you are counting 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F and not a six-decimal stablecoin that a wallet happened to place nearby.

sections.heading: Maker, not a rebrand of ARB
sections.body: Nothing in the ARB contract makes it DAI when it changes chains. This route sells ARB and can buy DAI. Circle and Tether are not the issuers of the output. If your treasury policy only allows fiat-issued stablecoins, Maker DAI may fail that policy even though it targets a dollar. Read the policy against the contract, not against the word stable.

sections.heading: Permission and fee live on chain id 42161
sections.body: Approve ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 if allowance is missing. The approval fee is ETH, not ARB and not DAI. You will not approve the Maker contract to receive DAI. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the short version of that split: permission on the source, credit on the destination. Keep the wallet on Arbitrum One while you sign the permission.

sections.heading: Wrong destination if ARB itself must survive
sections.body: This is the wrong page if you are trying to relocate ARB without selling it. The output is DAI only. It is the wrong page for Circle USDC, Ethereum Tether, WETH, and native ETH. It is the wrong page on Nova, and the wrong page if you wanted DAI on Arbitrum rather than on Ethereum. A same-chain swap would not show the Maker contract on Etherscan as the receive.

faqs.question: Is DAI issued by the Arbitrum protocol?
faqs.answer: No. The DAI contract 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is Maker's token on Ethereum. ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is a separate governance asset that you sell. Confirm DAI on Etherscan. Circle and Tether do not issue this output. If you need one of their contracts, this route will not satisfy the allowlist.

faqs.question: Do I keep voting power on the ARB I swap?
faqs.answer: No. Tokens you sell are no longer in the wallet. This route does not stake them and does not bridge them as ARB. Only the unsold remainder can still vote from this address on Arbitrum One. If a vote is imminent, reduce the size. The receive asset is Maker DAI, which has no ARB voting power.

faqs.question: What should I hold besides ARB before I start?
faqs.answer: Native ETH on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, for gas. The sentinel is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. ARB cannot pay the fee. You do not need DAI already on Ethereum to receive more DAI. You will need ETH on Ethereum later if you want to transfer that DAI, because DAI is not the mainnet gas coin.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to ETH on Ethereum. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and native ETH arrives here on Ethereum.

The sold contract is 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One. Check ARB on Arbiscan. Chain id 42161, not Nova. ARB is not gas. You pay the fee with native ETH already on that chain. The receive marker is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, meaning native ETH on Ethereum, chain id 1, not WETH. Etherscan shows that as an account balance. Blocks are about 12 seconds. The bridge does not promise to finish inside one block.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for native ETH on Ethereum. Output is the gas sentinel, not WETH. Check Arbiscan and Etherscan. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: Two different ETH balances, plus ARB
sections.body: You already need ETH on Arbitrum One to pay the fee. The ETH you can receive is a new balance on Ethereum. They do not net. Selling ARB does not refund the fee, and receiving mainnet ETH does not top up chain id 42161. If you spend your last Arbitrum ETH on the fee, that is expected. If you had no Arbitrum ETH to begin with, the ARB cannot move. The sentinel string looks the same in a quote. The chain id tells you which balance it names.

sections.heading: Native ETH is not the WETH contract
sections.body: 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is WETH on Ethereum. This route does not credit it. If your next step is an ERC-20 pool, you will wrap after arrival and spend a little of the new ETH on gas. If your next step is simply paying a mainnet fee, native ETH is the useful shape and WETH would have been the awkward one. Know which of those you are before you sign.

sections.heading: ARB price is the moving piece
sections.body: The amount of ETH is a market quote from a governance token into ether. It can change while the review sits open. Use the minimum. Request a fresh quote when the old one expires. Eighteen-decimal ARB versus eighteen-decimal ETH still does not mean one for one. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) is only the network you leave. Ethereum is where the gas coin can show up.

sections.heading: Wrong if governance tokens must remain
sections.body: Do not use this page to transport ARB. The output is ETH. Do not use it for Circle USDC, Tether, or DAI. Do not use it if you needed WETH specifically and cannot wrap. Do not use it on Nova. Do not use it if you meant to buy ETH inside Arbitrum One and never touch chain id 1. Those are all different receives.

faqs.question: Is the ETH I receive WETH in disguise?
faqs.answer: No. The receive marker is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, native ETH on Ethereum. WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. You sell ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. If a contract calls transfer on WETH, wrap first and leave gas. Etherscan will show the ETH as a balance change, not as that WETH token page.

faqs.question: I already have ETH on Arbitrum. Is that the destination?
faqs.answer: No. ETH on chain id 42161 pays the fee and stays on Arbitrum One. ETH that this route can credit is on chain id 1. Same ticker, separate balances. Arbiscan and Etherscan are the two explorers to watch. Nova is a third network and is not either side of this quote.

faqs.question: Does selling ARB for ETH keep my voting rights?
faqs.answer: Only on the ARB you do not sell. Spent units leave the wallet. They are not locked in a vote escrow by this page, and they do not reappear as ARB on Ethereum. The credit is native ETH. If you need the tokens for a proposal, lower the amount before you sign the quote.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to WETH on Ethereum. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and canonical WETH arrives here on Ethereum.

Spend 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548, the ARB token, on Arbitrum One. Arbiscan confirms it. Chain id 42161, not Nova. Gas is native ETH at 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and ARB cannot cover it. The receive contract is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Ethereum. That is WETH, an ERC-20, not the gas sentinel. Etherscan is the explorer. Chain id 1 blocks fall about every 12 seconds and do not time the route.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for canonical WETH on Ethereum. WETH is 0xC02aa, not native gas. Check both explorers first. Confirm both addresses on the explorers.

sections.heading: WETH9 on mainnet is a specific deployment
sections.body: 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is the canonical WETH contract traders expect on Ethereum. Arbitrum's own WETH, 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, is not what you sell and not what you receive. You sell ARB. If a quote or a portfolio substitutes one wrapped contract for the other because the ticker matches, stop and compare characters on Etherscan and Arbiscan.

sections.heading: You still need mainnet gas from somewhere else
sections.body: WETH does not pay Ethereum fees. If this wallet has no native ETH on chain id 1, the new WETH can sit idle. Unwrapping needs gas you do not receive here. That is a reason to prefer a native ETH output when the next action is a plain transfer. It is a reason to keep this output when the next action is a pool that only pulls the WETH contract.

sections.heading: Allowance on ARB, fee in ETH
sections.body: The permission, when needed, is an approval of 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on chain id 42161. ETH pays it. You do not approve WETH in order to receive WETH. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is enough background for that one-way permission. Keep a little ETH on Arbitrum One after the approval so the swap itself can follow in the same session.

sections.heading: Wrong when the output should be gas or ARB
sections.body: This page is wrong if you need native ETH on Ethereum immediately. It is wrong if you need ARB to remain ARB. It is wrong for Circle USDC, Tether, and Maker DAI. It is wrong on Nova. It is wrong if you meant to wrap ETH you already hold on Ethereum, which is a local call to the WETH contract and does not involve ARB at all.

faqs.question: Is canonical WETH the same as native ETH?
faqs.answer: No. This route can credit 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, which is WETH. Native ETH is the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and is not the output. You spend ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. One WETH is redeemable for one ETH only after you unwrap, and the unwrap needs gas you must already hold.

faqs.question: Am I selling Arbitrum WETH by mistake on this page?
faqs.answer: Not if the spend address is 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. That is ARB. Arbitrum WETH is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Check the approval screen against Arbiscan. If the wallet selected WETH, back out. Chain id 42161 must be active, not Nova. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Will WETH on Ethereum let me transfer it with no ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Moving an ERC-20 still costs native ETH on chain id 1. This route does not include that gas balance. If the account is new to Ethereum, fund a little ETH before you rely on the WETH. About 12 seconds is a block interval on Etherscan, not a schedule for either the bridge or a later transfer.

intro:
Swap USDC from Arbitrum One to USDT on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves Arbitrum One and BSC USDT arrives on BNB Chain.

You spend Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, six decimals, on Arbitrum One. Arbiscan is the check. Chain id 42161, not Nova, gas in ETH. The receive contract is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BNB Chain. Open it on BscScan. That USDT is the eighteen-decimal token widely used on chain id 56, not Ethereum's six-decimal Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Gas on BNB Chain is BNB. Blocks there are about 3 seconds, which is not a bridge schedule.
description: Swap Circle USDC on Arbitrum One for BSC USDT. The receive token has 18 decimals. Confirm both contracts on Arbiscan and BscScan. Read the minimum first.

sections.heading: Eighteen decimals on the way in
sections.body: A dollar of Circle USDC is six decimal places. A dollar of 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 is eighteen. The raw integers will not look alike even when the quote is fair. Read the USDT amount in whole tokens on BNB Chain, chain id 56, and confirm the contract on BscScan before you compare it with anything on Ethereum. Pasting the Ethereum Tether address into BscScan will not show this token.

sections.heading: Not a same-issuer hop
sections.body: Circle issued the USDC you sell. The BSC contract you can receive is not Circle's Ethereum USDC and it is not Arbitrum's Circle USDC. Treat it as the USDT deployment this route names, and verify the page on BscScan rather than assuming Circle redemption. If your treasury only accepts Circle's published native USDC list, check that list against 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 before you call the balance interchangeable.

sections.heading: ETH to leave, BNB to do anything after
sections.body: The fee on Arbitrum One is ETH. USDC will not pay it. After USDT shows up on BNB Chain, the next transfer or swap there needs BNB. This route's output is not the native gas sentinel, so it does not hand you BNB. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is the destination network, chain id 56, and an empty BNB balance will strand the new USDT until gas arrives another way.

sections.heading: Wrong if you needed Circle USDC to stay USDC
sections.body: This page does not deliver the Binance-Peg USDC contract 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. It delivers the USDT address above. It is wrong if you wanted six-decimal Ethereum Tether, wrong if you wanted BNB for gas, and wrong if you are holding bridged USDC.e instead of 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. Nova is the wrong source chain.

faqs.question: Is BSC USDT the same contract as Ethereum USDT?
faqs.answer: No. This route can credit 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BNB Chain, eighteen decimals. Ethereum Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, six decimals. You spend Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbitrum One. Confirm the receive page on BscScan, chain id 56, not on Etherscan. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Will this also give me BNB for gas?
faqs.answer: No. The output is the USDT contract, not the native sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Gas on BNB Chain is BNB. You need ETH on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, to start, and BNB on chain id 56 afterward if you want to move the USDT. About 3 seconds is a BNB Chain block interval, not a delivery promise.

faqs.question: I hold USDC.e. Can this quote see it?
faqs.answer: No. The spend is native Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. Bridged USDC.e is another contract on Arbitrum One. If that is the row with the balance, this quote will look short. Arbiscan should be open on the Circle address, with the wallet on chain id 42161, not Nova.

intro:
Swap USDC from Arbitrum One to ETH on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves Arbitrum One and pegged ETH arrives on BNB Chain.

Spend Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Nova. Arbiscan confirms it. Gas there is native ETH. What BscScan should show on the way in is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, Binance-Peg ETH, a BEP-20. It is not native ETH, not WETH on Ethereum, and not the gas sentinel. BNB Chain is chain id 56. Gas is BNB. Blocks are about 3 seconds and do not schedule the credit.
description: Swap Circle USDC on Arbitrum One for Binance-Peg ETH on BNB Chain. That ETH is a BEP-20, not gas. Check BscScan. It will not pay BNB fees. Confirm it.

sections.heading: Pegged ETH cannot pay BNB Chain fees
sections.body: 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is an ERC-20 style token on chain id 56. People call it ETH. The network calls the fee BNB. If you arrive with only this token, you still cannot send it until the wallet holds BNB. The sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE would have meant native BNB. This route deliberately does not use that marker. Do not unwrap it as if it were WETH9 on Ethereum.

sections.heading: Do not paste the Ethereum WETH address
sections.body: Canonical WETH on Ethereum is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. It does not exist as the receive asset here. Arbitrum WETH is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 and is not what you sell either. You sell Circle USDC. BscScan's token page for 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is the identity check. A ticker match against mainnet ETH is how funds get labeled and then stuck.

sections.heading: Dollar in, ether-linked token out
sections.body: Circle USDC targets a dollar. Pegged ETH tracks ether, with the peg and pool risks of that BEP-20. The minimum can move. Refresh a stale quote. Six decimals on the USDC you spend are not the decimals of the BEP-20 you receive. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is background for the chain change. It does not turn this BEP-20 into the gas coin of chain id 56.

sections.heading: Wrong page if you needed BNB or mainnet ETH
sections.body: Choose another route if the wallet on BNB Chain needs native BNB. Choose another route if you wanted ETH on Ethereum, chain id 1. This credit lives on chain id 56 only. It is also the wrong page if you hold USDC.e rather than 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, or if you wanted BSC USDT or Binance-Peg USDC instead of the ETH peg.

faqs.question: Is Binance-Peg ETH the same as native ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH is the gas coin on Ethereum and on Arbitrum One. On this route the output is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, a BEP-20 on BNB Chain. It does not pay gas. Gas there is BNB. Confirm the token on BscScan. Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is a third, separate contract.

faqs.question: What do I spend, and on which explorer?
