faqs.answer: Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbitrum One. Arbiscan is the explorer, chain id 42161, not Nova. You need native ETH there for the fee. The pegged ETH token is only the receive side, on chain id 56. About 3 seconds is a BNB Chain block time, not a promise for when the BEP-20 appears.

faqs.question: Can I use this ETH peg to pay a BNB Chain swap?
faqs.answer: Not as gas. You can sell the BEP-20 later if a pool lists it, but the transaction fee is BNB. If the account has no BNB, the pegged ETH sits until you add gas. This route does not include the sentinel that would have delivered native BNB. Fund BNB separately before you rely on the token.

intro:
Swap USDC from Arbitrum One to BNB on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves Arbitrum One and native BNB arrives on BNB Chain.

Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 is the spend on Arbitrum One. Check Arbiscan. Chain id 42161, not Nova. The fee there is ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on that chain. The same sentinel on the destination means native BNB, the gas coin of BNB Chain, chain id 56. BscScan shows it as an account balance, not as a BEP-20 supply. Blocks are about 3 seconds. That is not a fill time.
description: Swap Circle USDC on Arbitrum One for native BNB on BNB Chain. BNB is the gas coin, chain id 56. Confirm it on BscScan. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: The sentinel changes meaning with the chain
sections.body: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is not one token. On Arbitrum One it is ETH, which you must already hold for fees. On BNB Chain it is BNB, which this route can credit. If you copy the hex into a token search on BscScan, you will not find a normal BEP-20. Watch the account's BNB balance instead. Binance-Peg ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is a different asset and is not this output.

sections.heading: Useful when the next action needs gas
sections.body: People take this route when a BNB Chain wallet has tokens but cannot move them. Native BNB is what pays those fees. It is a volatile coin against Circle USDC, so the minimum matters. Do not assume a dollar of USDC becomes a fixed slice of BNB. Refresh the quote if it expires. Six-decimal USDC in, eighteen-decimal BNB out, and the human amounts on the quote are the ones to read.

sections.heading: Source fee is still ETH
sections.body: Arriving BNB does not pay the Arbitrum transaction that starts the route. Keep ETH on chain id 42161. USDC may need an approval, and that approval needs gas too. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) keeps those two payments straight: ETH where you sign, BNB where you land. Nova cannot supply the source fee.

sections.heading: Wrong if you wanted a dollar token on BSC
sections.body: This page will not deliver BSC USDT at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 or Binance-Peg USDC at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. It will not deliver pegged ETH. It is wrong if you wanted Circle USDC to remain a stablecoin, wrong if you hold USDC.e, and wrong if you thought BNB on this page was an ERC-20 you must approve on the destination.

faqs.question: Is native BNB the same as Binance-Peg ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Native BNB is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 56. Binance-Peg ETH is the BEP-20 at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. This route can credit BNB, not that peg. You spend Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. Check BscScan for the BNB balance, not for a token contract at the sentinel.

faqs.question: Do I approve BNB on BNB Chain to receive it?
faqs.answer: No. Native BNB is not an ERC-20 you approve in order to receive. Any approval happens on Arbitrum One for Circle USDC, paid in ETH. Chain id 42161, not Nova. Arbiscan should show 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. About 3 seconds is the typical BNB Chain block, not a schedule for the credit.

faqs.question: Why might the BNB amount differ from the dollars I typed?
faqs.answer: BNB floats against the dollar. Circle USDC does not. Fees and price sit between them. Use the minimum on the quote, and replace the quote if it expires. Decimals differ too: USDC has six, BNB has eighteen. Compare whole tokens. This page is the wrong one if you needed a stablecoin to arrive instead of gas.

intro:
Swap USDT from Arbitrum One to USDC on BNB Chain. Tether USDT leaves Arbitrum One and BSC USDC arrives on BNB Chain.

Sell Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbitrum One, six decimals. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Gas is ETH. The receive contract is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BNB Chain. BscScan lists that token as Binance-Peg USDC, eighteen decimals. It is not Circle's native USDC on Ethereum or Arbitrum, and Circle's published native list does not treat this as the same contract. Chain id 56, gas in BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. That block time is not a credit promise.
description: Swap Tether USDT on Arbitrum One for Binance-Peg USDC on BNB Chain. It is 18 decimals, not Circle native USDC. Check BscScan. Match the receive address.

sections.heading: Binance-Peg USDC is not Circle native
sections.body: Circle's USDC on Arbitrum One is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. You are not selling that here, and you are not receiving it. You sell Tether and you can receive 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. If a desk redeems only through Circle's native contracts, this BSC balance may not be on that list. Read BscScan and the issuer notes before you tell anyone you hold Circle USDC.

sections.heading: Six decimals sold, eighteen bought
sections.body: Arbitrum USDT uses six decimals. The pegged USDC on chain id 56 uses eighteen. A raw unit comparison will look like a huge surplus or a huge loss. Use the token amounts on the quote. Also remember both tickers say a dollar and the issuers differ, so the minimum can slip off one-for-one. If that slip is too wide, do not sign. Request a new quote rather than arguing with an expired minimum.

sections.heading: BNB is still required after a stablecoin arrives
sections.body: Pegged USDC does not pay gas on BNB Chain. Native BNB does, and the sentinel would have been the way to ask for it. This output is a BEP-20. Keep ETH on Arbitrum One for the Tether approval. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) will hold the pegged dollars only if chain id 56 is the network you gave as the destination.

sections.heading: Wrong for Tether fans and for Circle native fans
sections.body: This page is wrong if you wanted BSC USDT at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955, because the ticker changes to USDC. It is wrong if you wanted Ethereum Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. It is wrong if your balance is not 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, and wrong on Nova.

faqs.question: Is the USDC on BNB Chain issued as Circle native USDC?
faqs.answer: The contract this route names is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, Binance-Peg USDC, eighteen decimals. That is not Circle's Arbitrum USDC and not Circle's Ethereum USDC. Confirm the page on BscScan. You spend Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbitrum One. If you need Circle's native contract, this receive address is the wrong one.

faqs.question: Why is one dollar such a different integer?
faqs.answer: Six decimals on Arbitrum USDT, eighteen on the BSC USDC contract. The quote should display whole tokens. Do not subtract the raw base units and call the gap a fee. There can still be a real price gap because the issuers differ. Read the minimum.

faqs.question: Does this route pay the BNB Chain fee for me?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on chain id 56 is native BNB, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and this output is a BEP-20. You need ETH on Arbitrum One to start. You need BNB afterward if you will move the pegged USDC. Arbiscan is only for the Tether spend on chain id 42161.

intro:
Swap USDT from Arbitrum One to ETH on BNB Chain. Tether USDT leaves Arbitrum One and pegged ETH arrives on BNB Chain.

Tether on the way out is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. Arbiscan, Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Nova. Fee in native ETH. Pegged ETH on the way in is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. BscScan should show that BEP-20. It is not native ETH and not the BNB gas sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. BNB Chain is chain id 56. Blocks about every 3 seconds. Do not use that interval as a delivery clock.
description: Swap Tether USDT on Arbitrum One for Binance-Peg ETH at 0x2170 on BNB Chain. It is not native ETH. Verify it on BscScan. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: A BEP-20 that wears the ETH ticker
sections.body: 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is Binance-Peg Ethereum Token. Holding it is not the same as holding ETH on Ethereum, and it is not WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. You cannot pay a BNB Chain fee with it. You cannot deposit it to an exchange ETH address on Ethereum and expect credit. The chain id on the deposit page has to be 56, and the token contract has to match, or the deposit instructions are for a different asset.

sections.heading: Tether in, ether exposure out
sections.body: Six-decimal USDT goes in. The pegged token comes out at whatever price the quote shows. That price moves. The minimum is your bound. Arbitrum Tether is not BSC USDT at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955, so do not expect the same contract to appear on BscScan as both sides. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the chain-change primer. The asset change is separate: you are not bridging USDT unchanged.

sections.heading: Fee token on the source stays ETH
sections.body: Even though the destination ticker says ETH, the fee you pay at the start is native ETH on Arbitrum One, not the BEP-20. Keep that gas balance. USDT may need an approval on chain id 42161. After arrival, budget BNB if you will touch the pegged token. An account with only 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 cannot sign its own transfer.

sections.heading: Wrong for native BNB and for real mainnet ETH
sections.body: If you needed gas on BNB Chain, you wanted the sentinel, not this BEP-20. If you needed ETH on chain id 1, this page never goes there. If you needed USDC on BSC, the pegged USDC contract is a different address. If your USDT is not 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, or the wallet says Nova, stop.

faqs.question: Will an Ethereum exchange deposit credit this ETH?
faqs.answer: Only if that deposit is specifically for Binance-Peg ETH on BNB Chain, contract 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. A normal Ethereum ETH deposit address expects native ETH on chain id 1. Sending a BEP-20, or expecting this route to create mainnet ETH, is the wrong use. Read the exchange's chain and contract.

faqs.question: Is this the WETH contract from Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. The output here is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on chain id 56. You spend Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbitrum One. Native gas on BNB Chain is BNB, not this peg. Confirm the BEP-20 on BscScan before you sign. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: What gas do I need on each side?
faqs.answer: ETH on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, to sell USDT. BNB on BNB Chain afterward if you want to move the pegged ETH. The route does not deliver the BNB sentinel. About 3 seconds is a block interval on chain id 56. It is not a promise that the BEP-20 is already in the wallet.

intro:
Swap USDT from Arbitrum One to BNB on BNB Chain. Tether USDT leaves Arbitrum One and native BNB arrives on BNB Chain.

Spend 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, Tether on Arbitrum One. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Keep native ETH for the fee. Receive native BNB, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on BNB Chain, chain id 56. That is the gas coin, not a BEP-20, and not Binance-Peg ETH. BscScan shows the account balance. Blocks are about 3 seconds. The bridge is not obliged to match that pace.
description: Swap Tether USDT on Arbitrum One for native BNB on BNB Chain. BNB is gas, chain id 56, not pegged ETH. Check BscScan. Confirm both addresses on the explorers.

sections.heading: Ask for BNB only when you want the gas coin
sections.body: The sentinel on chain id 56 means BNB. It does not mean 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, and it does not mean BSC USDT. If a dapp needs the ETH peg, this credit will not satisfy a transferFrom call on that BEP-20. If a dapp needs to pay a fee, native BNB is exactly the balance that was missing. Match the goal to the marker before you sign.

sections.heading: Stable in, volatile gas out
sections.body: Tether aims at a dollar. BNB does not. The amount of BNB is a live quote. Minimums expire. Six decimals on the way out of Arbitrum and eighteen on BNB mean you should read human units. Do not line up base integers from Arbiscan and BscScan and invent a rate. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is chain id 56. Confirm the wallet network on the destination is that chain, not Ethereum and not Arbitrum.

sections.heading: Source approval still uses ETH
sections.body: USDT is an ERC-20 on Arbitrum One, so allowance may be required on 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. The fee is ETH, sentinel on chain id 42161, which is a different meaning of the same hex you see for BNB. Keep those meanings apart. You do not approve native BNB in order to receive it. There is no ERC-20 approval step on the destination for the gas coin.

sections.heading: Wrong for anyone keeping a dollar balance
sections.body: Skip this page if the destination should stay in USDT or move to Binance-Peg USDC. Skip it if you wanted pegged ETH. Skip it if you wanted BNB as a BEP-20 wrapper rather than the native balance. Skip it on Nova, and skip it if the USDT you hold is the Ethereum contract 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 rather than Arbitrum Tether.

faqs.question: Does the 0xEeee address mean ETH on BNB Chain?
faqs.answer: No. On BNB Chain the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means native BNB, the gas coin of chain id 56. Pegged ETH is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. You spend Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbitrum One. BscScan will show BNB as a balance, not as a token supply at the sentinel. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Will I receive BSC USDT if I start with USDT?
faqs.answer: No. The ticker changes. BSC USDT would be 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. This output is native BNB. If you wanted the dollar token to survive the move, this is the wrong page. Arbiscan is for the spend. About 3 seconds is a block interval on chain id 56, not a quote lock.

faqs.question: What fee token do I need before I sign?
faqs.answer: Native ETH on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Nova. Tether cannot pay that fee. The BNB you receive cannot pay it either, because it arrives on the other chain, and only after the signature. Leave ETH in the source wallet. Then use BNB for later actions on chain id 56.

intro:
Swap ETH from Arbitrum One to USDC on BNB Chain. Native ETH leaves Arbitrum One and pegged USDC arrives on BNB Chain.

Spend the gas sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Arbitrum One, which is native ETH, not WETH. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Leave a fee remainder in that same balance. Receive 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BNB Chain. BscScan calls it Binance-Peg USDC, eighteen decimals, not Circle's native USDC. Chain id 56, gas in BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. The block interval is not a fill promise.
description: Swap native ETH on Arbitrum One for Binance-Peg USDC on BNB Chain. Leave fee ETH. The USDC is not Circle native. Check BscScan. Read the minimum first.

sections.heading: You are selling the fee coin
sections.body: Native ETH on chain id 42161 pays gas and is the asset in the quote. The full balance will not clear. WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is untouched. If that wrapped row is what you hold, this page will not see it. Nova's ETH is a different chain. The sentinel hex will appear again on BNB Chain in other quotes, but there it would mean BNB. Here, on the source, it means the ETH you are selling.

sections.heading: Pegged dollars, not Circle's contract
sections.body: 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d is the BSC USDC token this route names. It uses eighteen decimals. Circle's native USDC on Arbitrum and Ethereum uses six, and those addresses are different. Do not tell a Circle redemption desk this balance is their native token until you have matched BscScan against their list. If the list does not include this peg, the route is the wrong tool for that desk.

sections.heading: BNB still missing after the credit
sections.body: Pegged USDC cannot pay a BNB Chain fee. If chain id 56 has no BNB, the new dollars wait. This quote does not attach a gas stipend. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is worth a look before you empty the source ETH and discover the destination cannot move. Price of ETH versus the peg can shift. Reread the minimum.

sections.heading: Wrong when you wanted ETH to remain ETH
sections.body: This output is not Binance-Peg ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, not native BNB, and not Ethereum USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. It is the wrong page for a local wrap, the wrong page for WETH holders, and the wrong page if you needed Circle's six-decimal USDC on Ethereum specifically.

faqs.question: Is this the Circle USDC I can redeem natively?
faqs.answer: Do not assume that. The receive contract is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, Binance-Peg USDC on BNB Chain, eighteen decimals. Circle's Arbitrum USDC is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 and is not the output. You spend native ETH on chain id 42161. Confirm the peg on BscScan and against the issuer you need.

faqs.question: Why can't I sell all my Arbitrum ETH?
faqs.answer: Because the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is both the asset and the fee on Arbitrum One. Gas has to remain. WETH will not cover that fee. Chain id 42161 is required, not Nova. About 3 seconds is a BNB Chain block interval on the destination and has nothing to do with how much ETH you must reserve.

faqs.question: Does pegged USDC let me transact on BNB Chain immediately?
faqs.answer: Only if the wallet already holds BNB for gas. The BEP-20 is not the fee token. Native BNB would have been the sentinel output, and this route does not use it. Fund BNB separately, or pick a route that delivers BNB, before you depend on moving 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d.

intro:
Swap ETH from Arbitrum One to USDT on BNB Chain. Native ETH leaves Arbitrum One and BSC USDT arrives on BNB Chain.

The spend is native ETH on Arbitrum One, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Not WETH. Chain id 42161, Arbiscan, not Nova. Reserve gas. The receive contract is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BNB Chain, eighteen decimals. BscScan is the explorer. That is not six-decimal Ethereum Tether. Chain id 56 charges BNB for gas. Blocks are about 3 seconds, and the bridge does not inherit that as a deadline.
description: Swap native ETH on Arbitrum One for 18-decimal USDT on BNB Chain. It is not Ethereum Tether. Reserve gas and check BscScan. Confirm the wallet network.

sections.heading: BSC USDT uses a different unit
sections.body: Ethereum Tether, 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, has six decimals and lives on chain id 1. This route can credit 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on chain id 56, with eighteen decimals. A wallet that imports the Ethereum address onto BNB Chain will not see this balance. Add the BscScan contract explicitly. Compare whole USDT on the quote with the ETH you are selling, and expect a market price, not a fixed redeem.

sections.heading: Leave ETH behind on the way out
sections.body: Selling the gas coin means the max button is a trap. Keep enough native ETH for the transaction on chain id 42161. Wrapped ether at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is a separate balance and will not be debited. If you only hold WETH, switch to a WETH route or unwrap first and still reserve a fee.

sections.heading: Destination gas is a different ticker
sections.body: USDT on BNB Chain does not pay fees. BNB does. This output is the token contract, not the sentinel, so you do not receive the fee coin. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) pages are the right place to remember chain id 56 before you paste a receive address from an exchange that only accepts a different USDT deployment.

sections.heading: Wrong for pegged ETH, BNB, or Circle USDC
sections.body: You will not receive 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. You will not receive native BNB. You will not receive Binance-Peg USDC at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. You will not receive Arbitrum Tether. The page is wrong on Nova and wrong if the goal was to keep ETH exposure rather than sell it for a dollar token.

faqs.question: Can I import Ethereum USDT on BNB Chain and see this balance?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum USDT is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. This route names 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on chain id 56, eighteen decimals. Check BscScan. You spend native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on Arbitrum One. The contracts are not substitutes. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Does the route include BNB for the next transfer?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on BNB Chain is native BNB. The output is a USDT contract, so a wallet with zero BNB can hold the tokens and still fail to send them. You must keep ETH on chain id 42161 to sign the sell. About 3 seconds is a block time, not a promise that both gas gaps are solved.

faqs.question: What if the wallet shows WETH instead of ETH?
faqs.answer: Then this is the wrong page. WETH is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. This quote spends the native sentinel on chain id 42161, not Nova. Unwrap only if you intend to sell ETH, and leave a fee. Otherwise open the WETH version of the route so the contract you hold is the one debited.

intro:
Swap ETH from Arbitrum One to BNB on BNB Chain. Native ETH leaves Arbitrum One and native BNB arrives on BNB Chain.

Both sides use the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and they are not the same coin. On Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, it is ETH, the asset you sell and the fee you must reserve. Arbiscan is the source explorer. Not Nova. On BNB Chain, chain id 56, the sentinel is BNB, the gas coin. BscScan shows a balance, not a BEP-20. Blocks there are about 3 seconds. That does not time the bridge. Pegged ETH is not involved.
description: Swap native ETH on Arbitrum One for native BNB on BNB Chain. Same sentinel, two gas coins. Confirm chain id 56 on BscScan. Review the minimum received.

sections.heading: One marker, two gas coins
sections.body: Quotes reuse 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE for whatever native coin the chain uses. Here the source native is ETH and the destination native is BNB. You are not moving ETH onto BNB Chain as ETH. Binance-Peg ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 would be that BEP-20, and this page does not deliver it. If a form asks you to paste the sentinel as a token address, the form is the wrong tool.

sections.heading: Do not sell the fee down to zero
sections.body: The ETH you sell is the ETH that pays for the signature. Leave a cushion on chain id 42161. WETH is not a stand-in. After BNB arrives, that new balance can pay later fees on chain id 56, which is often why people pick this pair. It cannot reach backward and pay the Arbitrum transaction. Order of operations matters.

sections.heading: Two volatile assets, no fixed ratio
sections.body: ETH and BNB both move. The minimum BNB is the number you are accepting, and it dies when the quote dies. Eighteen decimals on both natives still do not mean one ETH becomes one BNB. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) explains the hop. The price check is still yours, on this quote, before the signature.

sections.heading: Wrong if the ticker ETH must survive
sections.body: Anyone who needs the ETH peg on BNB Chain, or WETH on Ethereum, or a stablecoin, is on the wrong page. Anyone on Nova is on the wrong network. Anyone holding only wrapped ether on Arbitrum has the wrong balance selected. Anyone who thinks the identical sentinel hex proves the coins are the same object has misread the chain id.

faqs.question: If both addresses are 0xEeee, am I bridging ETH as ETH?
faqs.answer: No. The sentinel means native gas on whichever chain you are looking at. Source gas is ETH on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Destination gas is BNB on chain id 56. Pegged ETH, 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, is the BEP-20 people confuse with this output. BscScan will not show a token contract for the sentinel.

faqs.question: Should I keep any ETH on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: Yes. Enough to pay the fee. The route sells native ETH, so the entire balance cannot go. WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is not spent and does not pay gas. Nova is not chain id 42161. The BNB you receive later is only useful on BNB Chain.

faqs.question: Is a 3 second block the wait I should expect?
faqs.answer: No. About 3 seconds is how often BNB Chain produces a block. It is not a schedule for this route, and Arbitrum's faster soft blocks are not one either. If the quote expires, get another and read the new minimum BNB. The price between ETH and BNB can move while you wait.

intro:
Swap WETH from Arbitrum One to USDC on BNB Chain. Arbitrum WETH leaves and pegged USDC arrives on BNB Chain.

Sell 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, WETH on Arbitrum One. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. That contract is not the gas coin. Keep native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, for the fee. Receive Binance-Peg USDC at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, eighteen decimals, on BNB Chain. BscScan is the check. It is not Circle native USDC. Chain id 56 uses BNB for gas. Blocks about every 3 seconds, which is not a bridge timer.
description: Swap Arbitrum WETH for Binance-Peg USDC on BNB Chain. Spend 0x82aF, not native ETH. Confirm the peg on BscScan before you sign. Read the minimum first.

sections.heading: Approve the wrapped contract, not the gas row
sections.body: The allowance belongs to 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. If the approval screen shows the sentinel, you selected native ETH and this page is no longer the one you meant. Switch back. The approval costs ETH on chain id 42161. You do not approve the BSC USDC contract to receive it. An unlimited WETH allowance is more permission than a single trade needs. Set a cap when the wallet allows it.

sections.heading: Eighteen decimal peg versus wrapped ether
sections.body: WETH uses eighteen decimals. So does 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. That shared scale is not a one-for-one redeem, and the token is a pegged dollar, not Circle's six-decimal native USDC. Read whole tokens on the quote. Confirm on BscScan that you are not looking at BSC USDT by mistake. The issuers and the tickers both differ from the WETH you sold.

sections.heading: Gas after arrival is BNB
sections.body: The pegged USDC cannot pay chain id 56. Plan a BNB balance, because this route will not create one. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is the destination. The source still needs its own ETH. A wallet that holds only WETH on Arbitrum One will stall at the approval even when the WETH amount is large.

sections.heading: Wrong if the coins are still unwrapped
sections.body: Native ETH will not fund this quote. Neither will Binance-Peg ETH, which is not what you hold on Arbitrum. The page is also wrong if you wanted BSC USDT, native BNB, or Circle's Ethereum USDC. It is wrong if you wanted Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Nova is the wrong network for the WETH contract on Arbiscan.

faqs.question: Does this spend my ETH or my WETH?
faqs.answer: WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is the sold token. Native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, pays the fee on chain id 42161 and should not be the amount in the quote. If you hold only ETH, this page is wrong until you wrap. Arbiscan should show the WETH contract, not Nova.

faqs.question: Is BSC USDC the same as Circle USDC on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: No. Circle on Arbitrum is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, six decimals, and you are not receiving it. This output is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, Binance-Peg USDC, eighteen decimals. Check BscScan. If you need Circle's native contract, do not treat the peg as a substitute. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Can I move the USDC without BNB?
faqs.answer: No. BNB Chain fees are paid in BNB, and this route's output is the pegged token, not the gas sentinel. Add BNB before you rely on a transfer. About 3 seconds is a block interval on chain id 56. It does not supply gas and it does not lock the WETH price against the peg.

intro:
Swap WETH from Arbitrum One to USDT on BNB Chain. Arbitrum WETH leaves and BSC USDT arrives on BNB Chain.

The sold contract is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Confirm WETH on Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Pay gas in native ETH. The bought contract is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BNB Chain, eighteen decimals. Confirm it on BscScan. It is not Ethereum's six-decimal Tether and not Arbitrum Tether. Chain id 56, fee token BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. None of those facts is a promised credit time.
description: Swap Arbitrum WETH for 18-decimal USDT on BNB Chain. Receive 0x55d398, not Ethereum Tether. Check Arbiscan and BscScan. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: Do not import the wrong USDT
sections.body: Three Tether-like addresses show up in this corridor. Arbitrum USDT is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. Ethereum USDT is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. This route can credit only 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on chain id 56. Eighteen decimals, BscScan. If an exchange deposit says ERC-20 USDT on Ethereum, it is not asking for this balance. Matching the ticker is not enough.

sections.heading: WETH allowance, ETH fee
sections.body: Approve 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 if the allowance is empty. The fee is the sentinel balance on Arbitrum One. Selling WETH does not reduce the need for that fee. If you unwrap WETH to pay gas, you may unwrap the inventory you meant to sell. Leave both rows funded: a little ETH, and the WETH you want to trade.

sections.heading: Price, then a stranded token if BNB is missing
sections.body: Wrapped ether into a dollar token is a sale. Read the minimum USDT and refresh when the quote expires. After the credit, BNB is what moves the token. This page does not deliver the sentinel on chain id 56. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) covers the hop. It does not add a gas coin you did not select.

sections.heading: Wrong for native ETH sellers and for USDC buyers
sections.body: If the balance is unwrapped ETH, use the ETH route, not this one. If you wanted Binance-Peg USDC, native BNB, or pegged ETH, the output address will not match. If you wanted USDT to remain on Arbitrum One, you should not be looking at BscScan at all. Nova will not line up with the WETH contract this page spends.

faqs.question: Which USDT contract is the destination?
faqs.answer: 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BNB Chain, eighteen decimals. Check BscScan. Arbitrum Tether and Ethereum Tether are different addresses and are not the credit. You spend WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on chain id 42161. A deposit page that names another USDT is the wrong destination for this balance. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Is WETH going to arrive as pegged ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Pegged ETH is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. This output is the USDT contract above. Starting with wrapped ether does not mean the route preserves an ETH ticker. If you wanted that BEP-20, open the route that names it. Native BNB is the sentinel, and it is not the output either.

faqs.question: What two balances does Arbitrum need?
faqs.answer: WETH to sell, and native ETH to pay gas. The sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is only the fee on chain id 42161. Without it, the approval of 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 cannot go out. On the far side you will later want BNB, which this USDT credit does not include. Nova is not the source.

intro:
Swap WETH from Arbitrum One to ETH on BNB Chain. Arbitrum WETH leaves and pegged ETH arrives on BNB Chain.

Spend 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbitrum One. That is WETH, checked on Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Fee in native ETH. Receive 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, Binance-Peg ETH, a BEP-20 on BNB Chain. BscScan is the explorer. It is not native BNB, not the sentinel, and not Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Chain id 56, gas in BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. No promised credit time follows from that.
description: Swap Arbitrum WETH for Binance-Peg ETH on BNB Chain. Output is 0x2170, a BEP-20, not BNB and not mainnet WETH. Check BscScan before you sign the quote.

sections.heading: Three ETH-like contracts, one of them is yours
sections.body: Arbitrum WETH is what you sell. Ethereum WETH is a mainnet contract this route never touches. Binance-Peg ETH is what can arrive. They share a story about ether and almost nothing else: different chain ids, different addresses, different roles. Write the three addresses down if you are moving size. 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 out. 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 in. 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is the one you should not expect to see.

sections.heading: A peg is not a withdraw button
sections.body: Unwrapping Arbitrum WETH returns native ETH on chain id 42161. It does not mint the BEP-20 on BNB Chain. This route is the one that can credit the peg, and the amount is still a quote, not a guaranteed one-for-one across chains. Read the minimum. The peg can also differ from the ETH price you watch on Ethereum. BscScan is where you verify the token you hold after the fact.

sections.heading: BNB for later, ETH for now
sections.body: The BEP-20 cannot pay chain id 56 fees. Hold BNB separately. The source approval of WETH costs ETH on Arbitrum One. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the right note if you assumed a wrapped token on one chain is already the wrapped token on the next. It is not.

sections.heading: Wrong for gas seekers and for mainnet WETH
sections.body: If you need native BNB, the sentinel route is the one to open. If you need canonical WETH on Ethereum, this page is aimed at the wrong chain. If you are holding native ETH rather than 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, the quote is aimed at the wrong balance. Nova is the wrong network in every one of those cases.

faqs.question: Is Binance-Peg ETH the same as Arbitrum WETH?
faqs.answer: No. You sell 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbitrum One. You can receive 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BNB Chain. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and is neither side. Confirm the receive token on BscScan. The peg does not pay BNB Chain gas. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap WETH on Arbitrum and land on BNB Chain?
faqs.answer: No. Withdraw on the Arbitrum WETH contract pays native ETH on chain id 42161 only. It does not create 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Use this route if the BEP-20 is the goal, and keep ETH for the fee. About 3 seconds is a BNB Chain block, not the unwrap, and not a bridge promise.

faqs.question: What is the native gas token on the destination?
faqs.answer: BNB, marked by 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 56. This route does not credit that sentinel. It credits the pegged ETH token. You need BNB already, or from another route, before you can transfer the BEP-20. Source gas remains ETH on Arbitrum One, not Nova. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

intro:
Swap WETH from Arbitrum One to BNB on BNB Chain. Arbitrum WETH leaves and native BNB arrives on BNB Chain.

Sell WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. It is an ERC-20, so allowance may be required. The fee is native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Arbitrum One. The same sentinel on BNB Chain means the BNB you can receive, chain id 56. BscScan shows that as a balance, not as Binance-Peg ETH. Blocks are about 3 seconds. That is not a schedule for the credit.
description: Swap Arbitrum WETH for native BNB on BNB Chain. BNB is the gas coin, not pegged ETH. Check 0x82aF on Arbiscan and BscScan. Confirm the wallet network.

sections.heading: Wrapped ether in, the other chain's gas out
sections.body: This route is for a wallet that holds WETH on Arbitrum One and needs BNB to operate on chain id 56. You do not receive 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. You do not receive BSC USDT or pegged USDC. The output can pay fees on BNB Chain once it arrives. It cannot pay the Arbitrum fee that starts the trip. Keep a little native ETH beside the WETH.

sections.heading: Allowance stays on the WETH contract
sections.body: Approve 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on chain id 42161 if asked. Do not approve a sentinel address. Native BNB is not an ERC-20 you must permission on the way in. If the wallet is on Nova, the Arbiscan contract for One will not match the network you are signing. Change networks before the approval, not after a failed simulation.

sections.heading: No fixed WETH to BNB rate
sections.body: Both assets move. The minimum BNB on the quote is the floor, and it expires. Eighteen decimals on each side still do not mean equal amounts. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is where the gas coin will be useful. Read the destination chain id as 56 before you send the receive address from a form that defaults to Ethereum.

sections.heading: Wrong if you wanted the ETH peg to survive
sections.body: People who need Binance-Peg ETH should not be here. People holding native ETH rather than WETH should not be here. People who wanted a stablecoin payout should not be here. A local unwrap of WETH on Arbitrum One ends in ETH on chain id 42161 and never produces BNB. That unwrap is a different button.

faqs.question: Does this deliver Binance-Peg ETH or BNB?
faqs.answer: Native BNB. The destination marker is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 56. Pegged ETH is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 and is not the credit. You spend WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. BscScan shows BNB as a balance. About 3 seconds is a block interval, not a delivery promise. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Why do I still need ETH if I am selling WETH?
faqs.answer: Gas on Arbitrum One is native ETH, not WETH. The sentinel on chain id 42161 pays the approval and the swap. If that row is empty, 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 cannot move. The BNB you receive later lives on the other chain and cannot fund this signature. Nova is not a substitute gas network.

faqs.question: Is unwrapping WETH enough to get BNB?
faqs.answer: No. Unwrapping 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 returns ETH on Arbitrum One only. This page is what can credit native BNB on chain id 56. If you unwrap first, you then hold the gas coin, and you would need the native ETH route instead of this WETH route. Pick one path and match the balance you still have.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to USDC on BNB Chain. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and pegged USDC arrives on BNB Chain.

ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is the governance token you sell. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. It does not pay gas. Keep native ETH. The receive token is Binance-Peg USDC at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, eighteen decimals, on BNB Chain. BscScan is the check. It is not Circle's native USDC. Chain id 56 uses BNB for fees. Blocks are about 3 seconds and do not clock the route.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for Binance-Peg USDC on BNB Chain. ARB does not arrive as ARB. Confirm the peg contract on BscScan. Match the receive address.

sections.heading: Governance token sold, pegged dollar bought
sections.body: You do not receive ARB on BNB Chain. You can receive 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. Voting power leaves with the ARB you spend. The dollar token is a peg, eighteen decimals, not Circle's six-decimal native contract on Arbitrum at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. If a report needs Circle native USDC, this output will fail the address check even when the wallet says USDC.

sections.heading: ARB price is not a dollar peg
sections.body: The minimum USDC is a market number. It moves until you sign, and it dies when the quote expires. Eighteen decimals on both ARB and the pegged USDC do not make them equal. Read whole tokens. Do not compare base units from Arbiscan with base units from BscScan and call the difference a bug. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) will not freeze that price for you.

sections.heading: Two gas coins, neither of them ARB
sections.body: ETH on chain id 42161 pays the approval of 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. BNB on chain id 56 pays anything you do with the pegged USDC later. This route supplies neither gas coin as its output. The sentinel is not what you receive. Show up with ETH first. Plan BNB second.

sections.heading: Wrong if ARB must remain the asset
sections.body: Stop if you are trying to bridge the governance token unchanged. Stop if you wanted BSC USDT, native BNB, or pegged ETH. Stop if you wanted Circle USDC on Ethereum. Stop on Nova. Stop if you meant a same-chain sale into Arbitrum USDC, which would never show the Binance-Peg contract on BscScan.

faqs.question: Will I hold ARB on BNB Chain after this swap?
faqs.answer: No. You sell 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One. The asset that can arrive is Binance-Peg USDC at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. Check it on BscScan. It is not Circle's native USDC. Voting units you sell are gone. If you still need them, reduce the size. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Is this USDC eighteen decimals?
faqs.answer: Yes. 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d uses eighteen decimals on chain id 56. Circle USDC on Arbitrum uses six, and it is not the receive token. Read whole tokens on the quote. A raw integer will look enormous next to a six-decimal mental model. About 3 seconds is a BNB Chain block, not a reason to skip the decimal check.

faqs.question: What pays for the ARB approval?
faqs.answer: Native ETH on Arbitrum One, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, chain id 42161. ARB cannot pay it. BNB cannot pay it either, because BNB is on the other side and is not even the output. Add ETH before you sign. Add BNB later if you need to move the pegged USDC. Nova is the wrong source chain.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to USDT on BNB Chain. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and BSC USDT arrives on BNB Chain.

Sell 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Confirm ARB on Arbiscan. Chain id 42161, not Nova. Gas is ETH, not ARB. Receive 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BNB Chain. That USDT has eighteen decimals. BscScan is the explorer. It is not 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 and not Ethereum Tether. Chain id 56, fees in BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. The block time is not a fill time.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for 18-decimal USDT on BNB Chain. You do not receive ARB. Match 0x55d398 on BscScan before you sign. Confirm the wallet network.

sections.heading: The dollar token is BSC's USDT contract
sections.body: 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 is the receive address to memorize. Eighteen decimals. If you add Ethereum's 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on chain id 56, the balance will stay invisible. Exchange deposit pages that say ERC-20 USDT on Ethereum are a different asset on a different chain. This credit cannot satisfy them. Read the deposit chain as BNB Chain and the contract as the BscScan page.

sections.heading: You are exiting ARB, not relocating it
sections.body: The governance token is the input. It is not the output. Units sold cannot vote. There is no ARB balance created on BNB Chain by this quote. If the reason you opened a cross-chain page was to keep ARB and change networks, close this one. The minimum USDT is only a sale price, and it moves with ARB.

sections.heading: Fees bookend the trade
sections.body: Approve ARB with ETH on Arbitrum One. Move USDT later with BNB. Neither fee token is delivered here. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) uses chain id 56. The source explorer stays Arbiscan. Mixing them up is how an approval gets signed on Nova, where this ARB contract is not the same network.

sections.heading: Wrong for USDC, BNB, or pegged ETH
sections.body: Binance-Peg USDC is a different contract. Native BNB is the sentinel, not this page's output. Pegged ETH is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. None of those arrive. The page is also wrong if your token is Arbitrum WETH or native ETH rather than ARB. Check the spend address before you grant allowance.

faqs.question: Does ARB show up on BscScan after the swap?
faqs.answer: Not from this route. You spend 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One. BscScan should be checked for USDT at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. That token has eighteen decimals. If you needed the governance token itself, this sale is the wrong action. Voting power on the sold units ends. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Is BSC USDT six decimals like Ethereum USDT?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether is six decimals at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. The contract here is eighteen decimals. Read the quote in whole tokens. A base-unit copy will look wildly different. You still need ETH on chain id 42161 to sell ARB, and BNB later to move USDT. About 3 seconds is only a block interval.

faqs.question: Can ARB pay the Arbitrum fee?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, pays gas on chain id 42161. ARB may need an approval, and that approval needs ETH too. Arbitrum Nova is not the network. The USDT on BNB Chain will not reimburse the source fee. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to ETH on BNB Chain. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and pegged ETH arrives on BNB Chain.

The governance token 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is what you sell. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Keep ETH for gas. The BEP-20 you can receive is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. BscScan should show Binance-Peg ETH. It is not native ETH, not BNB, and not the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Chain id 56. Blocks about every 3 seconds. That cadence is not a delivery promise.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for Binance-Peg ETH on BNB Chain. The output is BEP-20 0x2170, not BNB and not ARB. Check BscScan. Check both explorers first.

sections.heading: Pegged ETH is not a gas balance
sections.body: 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 cannot pay fees on BNB Chain. BNB can. If you opened this page because a wallet was stuck without gas, you picked the wrong output. The sentinel route is the one that can credit BNB. This one credits a BEP-20 that still needs BNB before it can move. Exchange deposit pages for native ETH on Ethereum will not credit it either.

sections.heading: ARB is the only inventory this quote sees
sections.body: WETH, native ETH, and USDT balances on Arbitrum One are not inputs here. The approval, if it appears, names 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. If the screen shows another contract, you drifted onto another route. Selling ARB also drops voting weight. The ETH peg you receive has no governance rights in the Arbitrum DAO.

sections.heading: A float into another float
sections.body: ARB and ether both move, and the peg has its own market on BNB Chain. The minimum is the only bound, and it expires. Do not assume one ARB maps to a fixed slice of ETH. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) explains why the credit is not the same object you sent. Reread the BEP-20 amount on a fresh quote.

sections.heading: Wrong chain, wrong ticker, wrong job
sections.body: Wrong if you need native BNB. Wrong if you need ARB to stay ARB. Wrong if you need Circle or Tether dollars. Wrong if you need canonical WETH on Ethereum. Wrong on Nova. Wrong if you meant to wrap ETH you already hold on BNB Chain, which would not involve the ARB contract on Arbiscan at all.

faqs.question: Is the ETH on this route native or pegged?
faqs.answer: Pegged. The contract is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BNB Chain, a BEP-20. Native gas there is BNB, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. You sell ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Confirm the peg on BscScan. It will not pay fees and it is not Ethereum ETH. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Will my ARB voting power move with the peg?
faqs.answer: No. Sold ARB leaves the wallet on Arbitrum One. The pegged ETH token has none of that voting power. This route does not bridge ARB as ARB. If a vote matters, keep the tokens you need and sell only the rest. Chain id 42161 must be selected, not Nova.

faqs.question: What gas do I need besides ARB?
faqs.answer: ETH on Arbitrum One to sign, and BNB on chain id 56 if you want to move the BEP-20 after it arrives. This quote supplies the peg, not BNB. About 3 seconds is a BNB Chain block interval. It is not a promise that the peg has arrived, and it does not replace either gas balance.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to BNB on BNB Chain. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and native BNB arrives on BNB Chain.

Spend the governance token 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Check it on Arbiscan. Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Nova. ARB is not gas. Hold native ETH for the fee. Receive native BNB, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 56. BscScan shows a BNB balance, not a BEP-20 and not pegged ETH. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Do not treat that as the time the route owes you.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for native BNB on BNB Chain. BNB is gas on chain id 56, not pegged ETH. Confirm both explorers. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: A governance sale that refills another gas tank
sections.body: People use this pair when they need BNB and they are willing to sell ARB to get it. The output can pay fees on chain id 56. It is not 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 and it is not a stablecoin. It also does not appear on Arbitrum One to pay the fee you are about to sign. That fee is ETH. If the ETH row is empty, buy or bridge a little ETH first, then come back.

sections.heading: The sentinel is BNB only on chain id 56
sections.body: The same hex on Arbitrum One means ETH. Context is the chain id in the quote. You are not receiving ETH on BNB Chain. You are not receiving ARB. BscScan will not list a token supply at the sentinel. Watch the account's BNB figure. If a custodian asks for a BEP-20 contract address for the deposit, native BNB is the wrong asset to send them.

sections.heading: Price and voting weight both change

faqs.answer: The signature happens on Arbitrum One, and that chain charges ETH. BNB arrives later, on chain id 56, and cannot pay the earlier fee. The sentinel on the source is ETH, not a coupon for free gas. About 3 seconds is a BNB Chain block interval, not a waiver of the source fee.

sections.body: Polygon WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 is the page for ether on Polygon, not this one. Native POL is a different page. USDT is a different page. Nova is the wrong source. So is a wallet that holds only wrapped ether on Arbitrum One.

faqs.question: Which USDC contract should Polygonscan show?
faqs.answer: 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, Circle's native USDC, six decimals. It is not USDC.e. You spend native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. If a pool wants the bridged dollar, this credit will not match. Confirm the allowlist before you sign. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Why must I leave some ETH unsold?
faqs.answer: The sold asset is the fee asset on Arbitrum One. A zero remainder cannot pay gas. WETH is not a backup. Nova is not chain id 42161. The USDC you receive on Polygon does not refund this fee, and it does not become POL. About 2 seconds is a block interval, unrelated to how much ETH you reserve.

faqs.question: Does Circle USDC pay Polygon gas?
faqs.answer: No. POL does. The sentinel on chain id 137 is POL, and this route does not credit it. An older wallet may say MATIC for that row. Hold POL before you try to move 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. ETH on the source chain is a separate requirement. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

intro:
Swap ETH from Arbitrum One to USDT on Polygon. Native ETH leaves Arbitrum One and Polygon USDT arrives on Polygon.

Spend the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Arbitrum One, native ETH, not WETH. Chain id 42161, Arbiscan, not Nova. Leave gas. Receive Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygon, six decimals. Polygonscan is the explorer. That is not Circle USDC. Chain id 137, fees in POL, blocks about 2 seconds. The block interval is not a delivery clock.
description: Swap native ETH on Arbitrum One for Polygon USDT at 0xc2132. Tether, six decimals, not Circle. Reserve gas and check Polygonscan. Leave source gas ready.

sections.heading: Tether on Polygon is its own contract
sections.body: 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F is the USDT to verify. Arbitrum Tether, 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, is not what you spend and not what you receive. You spend native ETH. Six decimals on the way in mean a familiar dollar unit, not a familiar asset. Price still moves because ETH is the thing being sold. Read the minimum USDT again if the quote ages.

sections.heading: The max button spends your fee
sections.body: Native ETH on chain id 42161 is both inventory and gas. Keep a cushion. Wrapped ether will not fill in. If you unwrap WETH to reach this route, that unwrap is an extra transaction and also costs ETH. Do it only when the unwrapped balance is truly what you mean to sell.

sections.heading: Dollars that cannot pay POL
sections.body: After USDT arrives, transfers on Polygon need POL. A MATIC label is that native coin in many wallets. This output is an ERC-20, not the sentinel. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is useful before you empty Arbitrum ETH and discover chain id 137 cannot sign.

sections.heading: Wrong stablecoin, wrong gas coin, wrong wrap
sections.body: This is not Circle's 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 and not USDC.e. It is not Polygon WETH and not POL. It is not a way to keep ETH. It is the wrong page on Nova and the wrong page if the source balance is WETH rather than the sentinel. Before you sign, compare 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE with 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on their explorers and stop if either address on the quote differs. A stale minimum is a reason to ask for a fresh quote rather than signing the old one. The destination fee token is a different balance from the one this route can credit.

faqs.question: Is Polygon USDT the Arbitrum Tether contract?
faqs.answer: No. You can receive 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygon. Arbitrum Tether is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, and you are not spending it. You spend native ETH on chain id 42161. Confirm the receive token on Polygonscan. Six decimals do not make the addresses interchangeable. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Will I have POL to move this USDT?
faqs.answer: Not from this quote. POL is the gas coin on chain id 137, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. USDT is an ERC-20. Wallets may say MATIC for the gas row. Fund it separately. You must also reserve ETH on Arbitrum One because you are selling the fee coin. About 2 seconds is a block time, not a gas delivery.

faqs.question: What if I wanted Circle USDC instead?
faqs.answer: Then this page is wrong. Native Circle USDC on Polygon is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. USDC.e is yet another contract. This output is Tether. Check the quote's receive address against Polygonscan before you sign, and switch routes if the issuer does not match the app you are funding.

intro:
Swap ETH from Arbitrum One to WETH on Polygon. Native ETH leaves Arbitrum One and Polygon WETH arrives on Polygon.

Spend native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Arbiscan, not Nova. Reserve the fee. Receive 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Polygonscan should show WETH. The sentinel on Polygon would mean POL, not this token. Chain id 137. Gas is POL. Blocks about every 2 seconds. Unwrapping on Arbitrum would never create this address.
description: Swap native ETH on Arbitrum One for Polygon WETH at 0x7ceB. Polygon gas is POL, not this WETH. Confirm the contract on Polygonscan. Check both explorers first.

sections.heading: The sentinel is not the output on Polygon
sections.body: People see 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE in the source field and assume the destination is also native ETH. Polygon has no native ETH. Native gas there is POL. This route's output is the WETH contract 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. If you wanted POL, you are reading the wrong receive field. If you wanted Ethereum WETH, you are on the wrong chain.

sections.heading: A local wrap stays on Arbitrum
sections.body: Wrapping the sentinel on chain id 42161 mints 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 and stops. This page can credit a different WETH on chain id 137. The amount is a bridge quote, not the one-for-one function of a local wrap, because fees and the route sit in between. Read the minimum. Do not paste the Arbitrum WETH address into a Polygon pool and expect a balance.

sections.heading: You still need POL to use the WETH
sections.body: Arriving WETH does not pay Polygon fees. A wallet that says MATIC is talking about POL. Hold some, or the WETH is idle. On the way out, do not sell every wei of Arbitrum ETH. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the network that will list 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619, and only if chain id 137 is selected.

sections.heading: Wrong for dollar outputs and for gas outputs
sections.body: Circle USDC, USDC.e, and Polygon USDT are different pages. Native POL is a different page. Nova is the wrong source. A wallet holding only Arbitrum WETH is the wrong balance for this native ETH spend. Canonical mainnet WETH is not hiding inside the Polygon contract.

faqs.question: Does Polygon credit native ETH for this route?
faqs.answer: No. Chain id 137 has no native ETH gas. The output is WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. The sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Polygon means POL. You spend native ETH on Arbitrum One. Confirm WETH on Polygonscan. It cannot pay Polygon fees. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Is this the same as wrapping on Arbitrum One?
faqs.answer: No. A wrap there credits 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 and you stay on chain id 42161. This route can credit Polygon WETH instead. Reserve ETH for the source fee. About 2 seconds is a Polygon block, not the wrap function, and not a bridge promise. Nova is not either chain.

faqs.question: Why might the WETH amount differ from the ETH I sold?
faqs.answer: Because this is a cross-chain quote, not a local deposit into a WETH contract. Fees and price impact sit in the minimum. Read it. If the quote expires, the ratio expires. Do not assume one native ETH becomes one Polygon WETH down to the wei. Etherscan's WETH is a different contract entirely.

intro:
Swap ETH from Arbitrum One to POL on Polygon. Native ETH leaves Arbitrum One and native POL arrives on Polygon.

Both sides use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and they are different coins. On Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, it is ETH, which you sell and which also pays the fee. Arbiscan, not Nova. On Polygon, chain id 137, it is POL, the gas coin. Polygonscan shows a balance. It is not WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Blocks are about 2 seconds. That is not a bridge timer. Wallets may still say MATIC.
description: Swap native ETH on Arbitrum One for native POL on Polygon. Same sentinel, different gas coins. POL is not WETH. Check Polygonscan. Read the quote again.

sections.heading: Read the chain id beside the sentinel
sections.body: The hex does not identify the coin. Chain id 42161 means ETH. Chain id 137 means POL. This route sells one gas coin for the other. It does not move ETH onto Polygon as ETH, because Polygon does not use ETH as gas. If you needed the WETH contract, the sentinel output is the wrong shape. If a form asks you to paste 0xEeee as a token contract, decline. It is a marker.

sections.heading: Leave source gas, gain destination gas
sections.body: You must not sell the last ETH, or the signature fails. The POL you receive can pay later fees on Polygon, which is the practical reason to choose this pair. It arrives too late to pay Arbitrum. WETH on Arbitrum is not the balance being sold. If that is all you hold, wrap status matters: unwrap first, reserve a fee, then use this page, or pick the WETH route instead.

sections.heading: Two prices, no redemption rate
sections.body: ETH and POL both float. The minimum POL is the number to accept or reject. It expires. Eighteen decimals on both do not mean equal amounts. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) explains the hop between chain ids. It does not publish a fixed ETH to POL rate.

sections.heading: Wrong when the ETH ticker must remain
sections.body: Anyone who needs Polygon WETH, Circle USDC, or Tether is on the wrong page. Anyone on Nova is on the wrong network. Anyone who thinks a MATIC-labeled balance is a different asset from POL should still treat the native row as the output, not hunt a second contract. Anyone who wanted Ethereum mainnet ETH is on the wrong destination chain.

faqs.question: If both addresses are 0xEeee, do I receive ETH on Polygon?
faqs.answer: No. On Polygon the sentinel is POL, the gas coin of chain id 137. ETH is the sentinel only on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, where you spend it. WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 is not this output. Polygonscan shows POL as a balance. A MATIC label usually means that same native coin.

faqs.question: Should I keep ETH on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: Yes, enough for the fee. You are selling the fee coin, so the full balance cannot go. WETH will not pay that fee. Nova is not the source. POL that arrives later is useful on chain id 137 only. About 2 seconds is a Polygon block interval, not a reason to spend the last wei.

faqs.question: Is POL a stablecoin on this route?
faqs.answer: No. You are swapping two volatile gas coins. Read the minimum POL and refresh the quote if it lapses. If you wanted Circle USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 or Polygon USDT, this sentinel output is the wrong asset. Neither dollar contract is implied by the word swap.

intro:
Swap WETH from Arbitrum One to USDC on Polygon. Arbitrum WETH leaves the wallet and Circle USDC arrives on Polygon.

Sell 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. That is WETH, an ERC-20, on Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Native ETH, the sentinel, pays the fee and is not the sold amount. Receive Circle USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, six decimals, on Polygon. Polygonscan confirms it is not USDC.e. Chain id 137, gas in POL, blocks about 2 seconds. No credit time is promised.
description: Swap Arbitrum WETH for native Circle USDC on Polygon. Spend 0x82aF, receive 0x3c499c, not USDC.e. Check both explorers. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: The wrapped row is the inventory
sections.body: A wallet can show ETH above WETH. This quote debits only 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. If you approve the sentinel, you are on a different route. Allowance for WETH costs ETH. Cap it if you can. USDC on the receive side needs no approval to arrive. It may need approval later, and that later approval is a Polygon transaction paid in POL.

sections.heading: Native Circle, six decimals
sections.body: 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 is the contract to match. Bridged USDC.e will not increase. Tether's Polygon USDT will not increase. You are selling ether exposure for a dollar token, so the minimum is a price. Eighteen decimals of WETH against six of USDC make raw integers a poor comparison. Use the quote. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is where that Circle balance can live.

sections.heading: Three balances, three jobs
sections.body: WETH is sold. ETH on Arbitrum pays the source fee. POL on Polygon pays the next fee. This route fills only the first job's output, which is USDC, not POL. A MATIC label means the third balance. If it is zero, the USDC waits. Do not expect the bridge to invent gas you did not select.

sections.heading: Wrong when the coins are unwrapped or the dollar is bridged
sections.body: Native ETH needs the ETH route. USDC.e needs a different output than this page offers. WETH on Polygon is a different output. POL is a different output. Nova is the wrong chain. Ethereum Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 is the wrong network for the receive check.

faqs.question: Does this spend ETH or WETH on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: It spends WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, is the fee on chain id 42161. If you hold only ETH, this page will not see a balance to sell. Unwrap is a separate step. Confirm the WETH contract on Arbiscan, not on Nova. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Is the USDC native or USDC.e?
faqs.answer: Native Circle USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. USDC.e is a different contract, and this route does not credit it. Check Polygonscan. If your pool has not moved off the bridged token, the arrival will not show in that pool. Six decimals. Not Tether. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Will I be able to transfer the USDC immediately?
faqs.answer: Only if the Polygon wallet already has POL for gas. Chain id 137 does not accept USDC as a fee. Some wallets say MATIC for the native coin. This quote does not deliver the sentinel. About 2 seconds is a block interval, not a POL balance. You still needed ETH on Arbitrum to start.

intro:
Swap WETH from Arbitrum One to USDT on Polygon. Arbitrum WETH leaves the wallet and Polygon USDT arrives on Polygon.

The spend contract is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Fee in native ETH. The receive contract is Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F, six decimals. Polygonscan is the check. It is not Circle USDC and not the POL sentinel. Chain id 137. Blocks about every 2 seconds. That pace belongs to Polygon, not to the route.
description: Swap Arbitrum WETH for Polygon USDT at 0xc2132. Tether, not Circle, and not POL. Confirm the contract on Polygonscan before you sign. Read the minimum first.

sections.heading: Match Tether, not a generic dollar row
sections.body: Polygon wallets stack USDT, native USDC, and USDC.e in one list. This quote can credit only 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. If you tell a payer you are holding Circle, you will be describing the wrong issuer. Six decimals make the amount look like Ethereum USDT, but the address is not 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 and the chain is not Ethereum.

sections.heading: WETH allowance is the permission
sections.body: Approve 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbitrum One if asked. Pay with ETH. Do not approve USDT on Polygon in order to receive it. If the approval screen shows the gas sentinel, go back and select WETH. A Nova session will not line up with Arbiscan's One contract.

sections.heading: Sale first, gas second
sections.body: The minimum USDT is the sale price of wrapped ether. It moves. Refresh it. Afterward, POL is what spends that USDT. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) does not add POL to a route that selected Tether. A MATIC label is still the native fee token of chain id 137.

sections.heading: Wrong inputs and wrong outputs
sections.body: Unwrapped ETH is the wrong input. Circle's 0x3c499c contract is the wrong output. USDC.e is the wrong output. Polygon WETH and POL are wrong outputs if you wanted dollars. Keeping Arbitrum WETH and only changing chains without selling is a different intent this page does not serve. Before you sign, compare 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 with 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on their explorers and stop if either address on the quote differs. A stale minimum is a reason to ask for a fresh quote rather than signing the old one. Sign only on the source chain id named in this article, with the wallet network checked.

faqs.question: Which USDT address arrives on Polygon?
faqs.answer: 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. It is Tether, six decimals. Check Polygonscan. You spend WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbitrum One. Circle USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 is not the credit. Neither is Arbitrum Tether. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Does WETH on Arbitrum pay the Polygon fee?
faqs.answer: No. Source gas is native ETH on chain id 42161. Destination gas is POL on chain id 137, and this route does not deliver it. The sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means a different coin on each chain. USDT cannot substitute. About 2 seconds is a block time, not a fee.

faqs.question: What if my balance is native ETH, not WETH?
faqs.answer: This page will not sell it. The contract is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Use the native ETH route, or wrap first and still keep ETH for gas. Confirm the network is Arbitrum One, not Nova, before you approve. The receive asset remains Polygon USDT either way only if you are on the matching route.

intro:
Swap WETH from Arbitrum One to POL on Polygon. Arbitrum WETH leaves the wallet and native POL arrives on Polygon.

Sell 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, WETH on Arbitrum One. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Keep native ETH for the fee. Receive POL, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Polygon, chain id 137. Polygonscan shows a balance, not the WETH contract 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Blocks are about 2 seconds. That is not a fill time. Wallets may label POL as MATIC.
description: Swap Arbitrum WETH for native POL on Polygon. POL is gas on chain id 137, not Polygon WETH. Check Arbiscan and Polygonscan. Confirm the wallet network.

sections.heading: Wrapped ether becomes the other chain's gas
sections.body: This is the route when you hold WETH on Arbitrum One and need POL to unblock a Polygon wallet. You do not receive Polygon WETH. You do not keep an ETH ticker. The sentinel on chain id 137 is POL. If your wallet still prints MATIC, treat that native row as the destination. Do not search Polygonscan for a token contract at the sentinel hex.

sections.heading: Allowance on WETH, fee in ETH
sections.body: Approve 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 if the allowance is empty. The fee is the Arbitrum sentinel, which is ETH, not the WETH you are selling and not the POL you hope to receive. Unwrapping everything to manufacture gas can destroy the inventory this page needs. Leave both rows: a little ETH, and the WETH amount you intend to sell.

sections.heading: A market, not a wrap ratio
sections.body: WETH and POL both move. The minimum POL expires with the quote. Eighteen decimals do not mean one-for-one. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is chain id 137. Confirm the receive wallet is on that chain before you sign, not on Ethereum and not on Arbitrum One.

sections.heading: Wrong if ether exposure should remain
sections.body: Choose the WETH output if you need 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Choose a stablecoin output if you need dollars. This page is wrong for native ETH holders who have not wrapped, wrong for Nova, and wrong if you only wanted to unwrap WETH locally on Arbitrum One.

faqs.question: Is the output Polygon WETH or POL?
faqs.answer: POL. The marker is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 137. Polygon WETH is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 and is not the credit. You spend Arbitrum WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Polygonscan shows POL as a balance. A MATIC label usually means that gas coin. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Why is ETH required when I am selling WETH?
faqs.answer: Arbitrum One charges native ETH for gas, chain id 42161. WETH cannot pay it. POL cannot pay it either, because POL arrives later on the other chain. Keep a fee balance. About 2 seconds is a Polygon block interval and does not remove the source fee. Nova is not the network that holds this WETH contract.

faqs.question: Does unwrapping WETH give me POL?
faqs.answer: No. Withdraw on 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 returns ETH on Arbitrum One. This route is what can credit POL on chain id 137. If you unwrap first, switch to the native ETH route and still reserve gas. Do not expect the sentinel on Arbitrum to mean POL. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to USDC on Polygon. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and Circle USDC arrives here on Polygon.

Sell governance token 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. ARB is not gas. Hold ETH. Receive native Circle USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygon, six decimals. Polygonscan is the check. It is not USDC.e and not ARB. Chain id 137 uses POL for fees. Blocks are about 2 seconds. The route does not promise to finish on that interval.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for native Circle USDC on Polygon. Output is 0x3c499c, not ARB and not USDC.e. Check Polygonscan. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: You are selling voting weight for native USDC
sections.body: ARB spent from 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 cannot vote. Nothing on Polygonscan will show a replacement ARB balance from this quote. The dollar you can receive is Circle's native contract, not the bridged USDC.e many older pools still call USDC. If the pool has not migrated, your new balance will not connect to it. Check the pool's token address before you sell.

sections.heading: ARB does not have a dollar peg
sections.body: The minimum USDC is a market price. It changes, and it expires. Eighteen-decimal ARB against six-decimal USDC is another reason to read whole tokens only. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) will not lock the ARB price. Refresh the quote if you leave to check Polygonscan.

sections.heading: ETH to start, POL to continue
sections.body: Approve ARB with ETH on chain id 42161. Move USDC later with POL on chain id 137. A wallet that says MATIC is referring to that native fee. This output is not the sentinel, so POL is not included. Circle USDC will sit still in an empty gas wallet.

sections.heading: Wrong if the governance token is the point
sections.body: Do not use this page to transport ARB. Do not use it for Polygon USDT, WETH, or POL. Do not use it for USDC.e. Do not use it on Nova. Do not use it if you wanted Arbitrum's own Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 to be the receive contract. That address stays on the source chain's issuer list, not on Polygon.

faqs.question: Will ARB appear on Polygon?
faqs.answer: No. You sell 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One. The credit can be Circle USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. Confirm it on Polygonscan. It is not USDC.e. Voting power on the sold tokens is gone. Keep what you need for governance before you sign. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Is this the bridged USDC?
faqs.answer: No. Native Circle USDC is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, six decimals. USDC.e is a separate contract this route does not deliver. If your app still allowlists the bridged token, this page is the wrong dollar. You also need POL, not USDC, to pay gas on chain id 137.

faqs.question: What pays the ARB approval?
faqs.answer: Native ETH on Arbitrum One, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, chain id 42161. ARB cannot pay it. POL cannot pay it. About 2 seconds is a Polygon block and not a waiver of that fee. Nova is the wrong network for the governance token this quote spends. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to USDT on Polygon. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and Polygon USDT arrives here on Polygon.

Governance token 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is the spend. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Gas is ETH.
