description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for Polygon USDT at 0xc2132. You receive Tether, not ARB. Confirm the contract on Polygonscan before signing. Read the minimum first.

sections.heading: Tether's Polygon contract, not a bridged guess
sections.body: Memorize 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F if this is the balance you intend to hold. Six decimals. It is not native Circle USDC and not USDC.e. It is not Ethereum Tether. sections.heading: The sale ends the vote
sections.body: ARB you sell is not escrowed for a later proposal. It is not delivered as ARB. The minimum USDT is only as good as the quote. When ARB's price moves, that minimum moves with the next quote. Do not sign a floor you have not reread. Eighteen decimals on ARB versus six on USDT make base-unit math misleading.

sections.heading: Gas is never the governance token
sections.body: ETH on the way out, POL on the way in for any follow-up. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) places the approval on the source. The approval target is 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. If the screen shows WETH or native ETH as the sold asset, you have left this route.

sections.heading: Wrong asset if you needed Circle or ether
sections.body: Native USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 is a different issuer. WETH and POL are different exposures. This page is wrong for all three, wrong on Nova, and wrong if the point was to keep ARB while changing chains. Before you sign, compare 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 with 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on their explorers and stop if either address on the quote differs. Keep the source fee token in the wallet after you choose the trade size. Sign only on the source chain id named in this article, with the wallet network checked.

faqs.question: Does this bridge ARB itself onto Polygon?
faqs.answer: No. The spend is 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One. The receive can be Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. Check Polygonscan. You lose voting weight on the amount sold. If the goal was to hold ARB on another chain, this output is the wrong token. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Is Polygon USDT six decimals?
faqs.answer: Yes. 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F uses six decimals, like Ethereum Tether, but it is not that contract. Read whole tokens on the quote. You still need ETH to sell ARB on chain id 42161, and POL to move USDT on chain id 137. About 2 seconds is a block interval, not a decimal conversion.

faqs.question: Can I pay Polygon fees with the USDT?
faqs.answer: No. POL is the gas coin, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Some wallets label it MATIC. This route does not credit it. USDT is an ERC-20 that sits until POL is present. Source gas remains ETH on Arbitrum One, not Nova. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

intro:

Write down 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 and compare Polygonscan. The minimum is a cross rate between two volatile assets. It expires. Voting weight leaves with the ARB.

sections.body: Allowance, when required, is for 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on chain id 42161, paid in ETH. You do not approve Polygon WETH to receive it. sections.body: This output is not ARB, not Circle USDC, not USDT, and not POL. It is the wrong page if you meant to sell Arbitrum WETH rather than ARB. Before you sign, compare 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 with 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on their explorers and stop if either address on the quote differs. faqs.question: Is Polygon WETH native ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Chain id 137 does not use ETH as gas. The output is the ERC-20 at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. POL is the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. You sell ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Confirm WETH on Polygonscan. It will not pay fees. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Do I keep ARB on Polygon?
faqs.answer: No. This is a sale. The governance token stays behind only in the amount you do not spend. Polygon receives WETH, not ARB. If a proposal needs your tokens, lower the trade. Chain id 42161, not Nova, is where the unsold ARB remains. About 2 seconds is a Polygon block, not a voting extension.

faqs.question: Which WETH address is easy to confuse with this one?
faqs.answer: Arbitrum WETH 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 and Ethereum WETH 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Neither is the receive contract, and neither is the spend. The spend is ARB. The receive is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Compare full addresses on the two explorers. faqs.question: Does this keep my ARB voting power?

The approval, if needed, is for 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on chain id 42161. You do not approve native ETH on Base in order to receive it.

sections.heading: The 0x4200 predeploy is Base-specific
sections.body: OP-stack chains share the WETH address 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, and that does not make the balance shared. This quote can credit the predeploy on chain id 8453 only. sections.body: Base fees are native ETH. Receiving WETH does not create that balance. If the Base account has never held ETH, you can own WETH and still be unable to unwrap or transfer it. Unwrapping needs gas first. This route is the wrong shape when the next click is a plain Base transfer. It is the right shape when a contract calls transfer on the predeploy.

sections.heading: Dollars against wrapped ether
sections.body: Six-decimal Circle USDC goes in. Eighteen-decimal WETH can come out. The minimum is a price, and it expires. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) covers the hop between Arbitrum One and Base. It does not turn USDC into a one-for-one wrap. USDC.e on the source will not be accepted as the spend.

sections.heading: Wrong chain or wrong wrapper
sections.body: Stop if you need native ETH on Base for gas. Stop if you need Ethereum mainnet. Stop if you need Base USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. Stop on Nova. Stop if you meant to wrap ETH you already hold on Base, which is a local call and does not involve Arbitrum USDC.

faqs.question: Is Base WETH the Ethereum WETH contract?
faqs.answer: No. Base uses 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. You spend Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbitrum One. Confirm the predeploy on Basescan, chain id 8453. It is an L2 contract, not a mainnet balance, and it does not pay gas. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap Base WETH with a zero ETH balance?
faqs.answer: No. The unwrap is a transaction, and Base charges native ETH, the sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. This route does not credit that sentinel. If the account has no Base ETH, fund gas first or choose a route that delivers native ETH. About 2 seconds is a block interval, not an unwrap.

faqs.question: Does the shared 0x4200 address mean every L2 shares my WETH?
faqs.answer: No. The predeploy address is reused by design on OP-stack chains, but balances are per chain id. A credit on Base does not appear on another rollup that uses the same hex. Check chain id 8453 on Basescan. Arbitrum WETH is a different address entirely, 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, and you are not selling it.

sections.body: The issuer changes. Six decimals on both make the fee look small, and it can still be real. Read the minimum. Do not assume a desk that redeems Tether will redeem this USDC, or the reverse. Arbitrum Tether is not Base USDC with a new coat of paint. [Base](/chains/base) is chain id 8453, not Ethereum, so Etherscan is the wrong explorer for the receive.

sections.body: You need ETH on Arbitrum One to move USDT. You need ETH on Base later to move USDC. This output is not the gas sentinel, so the second balance is not included. Two rollups, two fee tanks. Nova is not a third name for either of them.

sections.heading: Wrong if you wanted Tether to remain

faqs.answer: Yes. Arbitrum USDT and Base Circle USDC are both six decimals, so whole-token amounts are comparable. They are still different issuers. Read the minimum rather than assuming one-for-one. About 2 seconds is a Base block interval, not a price lock. You need ETH on chain id 42161 to start.

faqs.answer: No. Base is an L2 that charges native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. USDC is an ERC-20. This route does not deliver the gas coin. Hold Base ETH before you transfer 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. Arbitrum ETH will not cover that Base fee. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

sections.heading: Gas on Base, bought with Tether
sections.body: Use this page when a Base wallet needs ETH to sign and you hold USDT on Arbitrum One. The output is the fee coin of chain id 8453. It is not 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. The ETH you receive on Base arrives too late to fund the signature, and it lives on the other rollup anyway. Nova is not a spare tank. If the Arbitrum ETH row is empty, fix that before you look at the USDT amount.

sections.heading: A dollar token into a volatile fee coin
sections.body: The minimum ETH moves with the market. Refresh the quote. Six-decimal USDT against eighteen-decimal ETH should be read in whole units. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) explains the rollup hop. It does not freeze ETH's price against Tether.

sections.heading: Wrong for wrapped ether and for staying in dollars
sections.body: If a Base contract wants the WETH predeploy, this native output fails the ERC-20 check until you wrap, and wrapping needs a bit of the ETH you just received. If you wanted Circle USDC on Base, this is the wrong ticker. If you wanted USDT to remain USDT, this page sells it.

faqs.question: Does this ETH show up on Ethereum mainnet?
faqs.answer: No. The receive network is Base, chain id 8453, an L2. The marker is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, native gas on Base. Etherscan is the wrong explorer. Basescan is the right one. You spend Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbitrum One. Mainnet ETH is a different balance on chain id 1.

faqs.question: Is this the same as Base WETH?
faqs.answer: No. Base WETH is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. This route credits the gas coin. Contracts that only pull WETH will not see it until you wrap. Leave a little ETH for that wrap. About 2 seconds is a Base block interval, not the wrap, and not a bridge schedule.

faqs.question: Why do I need ETH on Arbitrum if I am trying to get ETH on Base?
faqs.answer: Because the transaction that starts the route is on chain id 42161, and that chain charges its own ETH. Base ETH cannot pay it. Tether cannot pay it. Hold a source fee, then receive a destination fee. They are not one balance. Nova is not chain id 42161.

sections.heading: Predeploy versus the sentinel
sections.body: Base pools that say ETH often mean 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. The wallet's gas row is the sentinel instead. This route can credit the predeploy. It will not increase the gas row. If you import Ethereum's WETH address on Base, you will be watching an empty, wrong contract. The reused 0x4200 hex on another OP-stack chain is also not this balance.

sections.heading: You may be unable to touch what you receive
sections.body: Moving WETH costs native ETH on Base. A brand new Base account with only this credit cannot unwrap and cannot transfer. Plan a little Base ETH from somewhere else, or pick the native ETH output if gas was the real goal. Tether on the source still needs Arbitrum ETH before any of that matters.

sections.heading: Issuer and exposure both change
sections.body: Tether is a dollar token. WETH is ether exposure. The minimum is a price. It expires. Six decimals versus eighteen. [Base](/chains/base) is the destination L2, chain id 8453. Etherscan will not list this WETH balance. If you open the wrong explorer, you will think the route failed when it landed on Base.

sections.heading: Wrong for USDC, for gas, and for mainnet
sections.body: Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 is a different output. Native ETH is a different output. Ethereum mainnet is a different chain. Nova is the wrong source. Selling Arbitrum WETH is a different input. This page spends Tether only. Before you sign, compare 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 with 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on their explorers and stop if either address on the quote differs. Do not treat a block interval on either chain as a promise for when the credit appears. Gas on the source chain is separate from the asset you hope to receive.

faqs.question: What is the WETH address on Base?
faqs.answer: 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Confirm it on Basescan, chain id 8453. It is not Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and not native ETH. You spend Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbitrum One. The same 0x4200 hex on another rollup is not your Base balance. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Will this WETH pay Base gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 8453. WETH is an ERC-20. If the Base account has no ETH, you cannot unwrap. About 2 seconds is a block interval, not a gas balance. You also need ETH on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, to move the USDT.

faqs.question: Is USDT on Base the thing I receive?
faqs.answer: No. The output is WETH. If you wanted Circle USDC on Base, the contract would be 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, and this page does not name it. Starting with Tether does not mean the ticker survives. Read the receive address on the quote before you sign. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

intro:
Swap ETH from Arbitrum One to USDC on Base. Native ETH leaves Arbitrum One and Circle USDC arrives on Base.

Spend the gas sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Arbitrum One. That is native ETH, not WETH. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Reserve a fee in that same balance. Receive Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Base, six decimals. Basescan confirms it. It is not USDbC. Base is chain id 8453, an L2, blocks about 2 seconds. The interval is not a fill time.
description: Swap native ETH on Arbitrum One for Circle USDC on Base. Receive 0x833589, not USDbC. Reserve fee ETH and check Basescan. Review the minimum received.

sections.heading: You are selling one rollup's gas coin
sections.body: ETH on Arbitrum One pays the fee and is the asset in the quote. Do not enter the full balance. WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is not debited. The ETH people hold on Base is a third balance and is not spent here. Chain id 8453 will not shrink because you sold chain id 42161. If the wallet is on Nova, none of these balances match the signature.

sections.heading: Circle on Base, not the bridged dollar
sections.body: 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 is native USDC. USDbC is the older token. Apps differ on which they accept. Check Basescan against the app before you sell ETH into the one the app ignores. Six decimals. Not Tether. Not a gas coin. You will not receive the sentinel on Base, so you do not receive Base ETH from this page.

sections.heading: After dollars arrive, Base still wants ETH
sections.body: USDC cannot pay chain id 8453. If you sold your Arbitrum ETH and did not already have Base ETH, the new dollars wait. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is a reminder that each rollup has its own fee. The minimum USDC is also a price against ETH, so reread it if the quote expires.

sections.heading: Wrong if you wanted ETH to stay the gas coin
sections.body: Native ETH on Base is a different route. Base WETH is a different route. Mainnet is a different chain. This page is wrong for WETH holders on Arbitrum, wrong for anyone seeking USDbC, and wrong for a same-chain wrap that never leaves chain id 42161.

faqs.question: Which USDC should Basescan show?
faqs.answer: Circle native USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, six decimals, on chain id 8453. It is not USDbC. You spend native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on Arbitrum One. If the app wants the bridged dollar, this route delivers the wrong contract. Base is an L2, not Ethereum mainnet. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Why can't I swap my entire Arbitrum ETH balance?
faqs.answer: It is the fee coin on chain id 42161. The transaction needs a remainder. WETH will not cover the gap. Base ETH will not cover it either, because that balance is on chain id 8453. About 2 seconds is a Base block interval and says nothing about how much source ETH to reserve. Nova is the wrong network.

faqs.question: Does the received USDC include gas for Base?
faqs.answer: No. Base charges native ETH. This output is an ERC-20. The sentinel is not the receive asset. Hold Base ETH separately before you move 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. Selling Arbitrum ETH does not fill the Base gas row. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

intro:
Swap ETH from Arbitrum One to WETH on Base. Native ETH leaves Arbitrum One and Base WETH arrives on Base.

Spend native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on Arbitrum One. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Reserve the fee. Receive 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base. Basescan should show that predeploy. It is not Base gas and not Ethereum WETH. Chain id 8453 is an L2. Blocks are about 2 seconds. A local wrap on Arbitrum would not create this credit.
description: Swap native ETH on Arbitrum One for Base WETH at 0x4200. That is not Base gas and not mainnet WETH. Confirm the predeploy on Basescan. Read the minimum first.

sections.heading: Wrapping locally never leaves Arbitrum
sections.body: Deposit into 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 and you stay on chain id 42161 with Arbitrum WETH. This route can credit the Base predeploy instead. The amount is a quote, not the one-wei-for-one-wei result of a local deposit, because the hop has costs. Read the minimum. Do not paste the Arbitrum WETH address into Basescan and expect a balance.

sections.heading: The predeploy is not the gas row
sections.body: 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 cannot pay Base fees. The sentinel on chain id 8453 can. If this Base wallet has no ETH, the new WETH is stuck until gas arrives. You also cannot spend every wei on Arbitrum, because that chain's fee comes from the same balance you are selling. Two gas constraints, and the output helps with neither until you unwrap, which itself needs Base ETH.

sections.heading: Mainnet WETH is a different hex
sections.body: 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is Ethereum. This page never targets chain id 1. [Base](/chains/base) is the L2, chain id 8453. The 0x4200 address is reused on other OP-stack chains and the balances are not pooled. Check the chain id in the wallet header before you decide the credit is missing.

sections.heading: Wrong if you needed spendable Base ETH
sections.body: Choose the native output if the next action is a fee. Choose a USDC output if you wanted dollars. This page is wrong for WETH you already hold on Arbitrum, wrong for Nova, and wrong for a mainnet wrap. It is also wrong if you thought Base ETH and Arbitrum ETH were one balance that wrapping could reshuffle.

faqs.question: Is this just wrapping ETH?
faqs.answer: No. A wrap on Arbitrum One credits 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 and stays on chain id 42161. This route spends native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and can credit Base WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Check Basescan. It is an L2 predeploy, not Ethereum WETH. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Will Base WETH pay gas on Base?
faqs.answer: No. Gas is native ETH on chain id 8453. The predeploy is an ERC-20. Unwrapping needs ETH already in the account, which this route does not provide. About 2 seconds is a Base block interval, not a gas credit. Reserve ETH on Arbitrum One as well, because you are selling the source fee coin.

faqs.question: Does 0x4200 on another chain show this balance?
faqs.answer: No. The address is a shared predeploy pattern. The ledger is per chain. Only chain id 8453 can show this credit, on Basescan. Another rollup with the same hex is a different wallet balance. Nova is not Base, and it is not the source network either.

intro:
Swap WETH from Arbitrum One to USDC on Base. Arbitrum WETH leaves the wallet and Circle USDC arrives on Base.

Sell 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. That is WETH, not the gas sentinel. Keep native ETH for the fee. Receive Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Base, six decimals. Basescan should show it, not USDbC. Base is chain id 8453, an L2. Blocks about every 2 seconds. No fill time is implied.
description: Swap Arbitrum WETH for Circle USDC on Base. Spend 0x82aF and receive 0x833589, not USDbC. Check Arbiscan and Basescan. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: Approve wrapped ether, not the fee row
sections.body: Allowance belongs to 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. If the screen shows the sentinel, you selected native ETH and left this route. The approval costs ETH on chain id 42161. You do not approve Base USDC to receive it. Cap the WETH allowance when the wallet offers a limit. An unlimited permission on wrapped ether outlives this one quote.

sections.heading: Native USDC on the L2
sections.body: 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 is Circle on Base. USDbC is the bridged predecessor. Pools differ. Match the app to Basescan before you sell WETH into a dollar the app cannot see. Six decimals out, eighteen in on the WETH side. Read whole tokens. The minimum is a sale of ether exposure, not a fixed wrap.

sections.heading: Base ETH is still your problem
sections.body: USDC will not pay chain id 8453. This route does not deliver the sentinel there. Arbitrum ETH pays only the source. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) keeps those fees apart. If both gas rows are empty, fix Arbitrum first so you can sign, then fix Base so you can move the dollars.

sections.heading: Wrong balance, wrong dollar, wrong chain
sections.body: Native ETH on Arbitrum needs a different route. USDbC is the wrong receive if that is what you meant by USDC. Base WETH and native Base ETH are wrong receives if you wanted dollars to stop being ether. Mainnet is the wrong destination. Nova is the wrong source.

faqs.question: Does this route sell my Arbitrum ETH?
faqs.answer: Only as gas. The trade size is WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. The sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is the fee on chain id 42161. If you hold only ETH, this quote cannot see it. Confirm the WETH contract on Arbiscan, not Nova. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Is Base USDC the bridged USDbC token?
faqs.answer: No. The receive contract is 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, Circle's native USDC, six decimals. USDbC is different. Check Basescan, chain id 8453. If your pool has not migrated, this credit will not connect. Base is an L2. Etherscan will not show the balance. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Can I transfer that USDC without Base ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Chain id 8453 charges native ETH. USDC is not the fee token, and this route does not include the sentinel on Base. About 2 seconds is a block interval, not a gas drop. Keep ETH on Arbitrum to start, and ETH on Base to finish the next transfer.

intro:
Swap WETH from Arbitrum One to ETH on Base. Arbitrum WETH leaves the wallet and native ETH arrives on Base.

Sell 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbitrum One. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. The fee is native ETH on that same chain, a different row. Receive native ETH on Base, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, chain id 8453. Basescan shows a balance, not the predeploy 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Base is an L2. Blocks about 2 seconds. Unwrapping on Arbitrum does not produce this balance.
description: Swap Arbitrum WETH for native ETH on Base. Output is Base gas, not the 0x4200 predeploy. Confirm the balance on Basescan. Review the minimum received.

sections.heading: Unwrap and bridge are different buttons
sections.body: Withdraw on Arbitrum WETH returns ETH on chain id 42161. You stay home. This page can credit ETH on Base instead. The sentinel hex is on both sides of the quote and means a different chain's gas each time. Source sentinel: fee, not the sold token. Destination sentinel: the coin you can receive. If you wanted the predeploy, the gas coin is the wrong shape.

sections.heading: Useful when Base cannot sign
sections.body: A Base account with tokens and no ETH is stuck. Native ETH fixes that. WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 would not. Do not confuse the two after the credit lands. Basescan's balance, not a token page, is the check. Mainnet ETH will not appear. Chain id 1 is not involved.

sections.heading: Keep a little source ETH beside the WETH
sections.body: The approval of 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 costs ETH on Arbitrum One. If you unwrap all WETH first, you no longer hold the contract this route spends, and you should switch to the native ETH route instead. [Base](/chains/base) is only the destination. The signature still happens on chain id 42161.

sections.heading: Wrong for the predeploy and for dollars
sections.body: Stop if a pool wants 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Stop if you wanted Circle USDC. Stop if you are holding native ETH rather than WETH. Stop on Nova. Stop if you thought Arbitrum ETH and Base ETH were already the same object and this page was only a label change.

faqs.question: Do I receive Base WETH or Base ETH?
faqs.answer: Native ETH. The output marker is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 8453. The WETH predeploy is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 and is not the credit. You spend 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Check the Base balance on Basescan. It can pay gas. The predeploy cannot. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Will unwrapping Arbitrum WETH put ETH on Base?
faqs.answer: No. It returns ETH on Arbitrum One only. This route is the one that can credit Base. If you already unwrapped, use the native ETH input route and reserve a fee. About 2 seconds is a Base block, not the unwrap, and not a promise. Nova is neither side.

faqs.question: Why does the sentinel appear twice?
faqs.answer: It means native gas on each chain. On Arbitrum One it is the ETH you use as a fee while selling WETH. On Base it is the ETH you can receive. Same hex, chain id 42161 versus 8453. It is not Ethereum mainnet in either field. Etherscan is the wrong explorer for the credit.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to USDC on Base. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and Circle USDC arrives here on Base.

Sell 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548, the governance token. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. ARB is not gas. Hold ETH. Receive Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Base, six decimals. Basescan confirms it is not USDbC and not ARB. Base is chain id 8453, an L2. Blocks about every 2 seconds. That is not a schedule for the sale.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for Circle USDC on Base. You receive 0x833589, not ARB and not USDbC. Check Basescan before you sign. Match the receive address.

sections.heading: Voting weight leaves, native USDC can arrive
sections.body: Spent ARB does not vote and does not reappear on Base. The dollar is Circle's native contract on chain id 8453. Bridged USDbC is a different address that some apps still hard-code. If you are funding one of those apps, this route is the wrong dollar even though the wallet will say USDC. Match the app to Basescan first.

sections.heading: A float priced in six-decimal dollars
sections.body: ARB has eighteen decimals and no peg. USDC has six and a dollar target. The minimum is the only bound, and it expires when the quote does. Do not compare raw integers across those scales. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) will not freeze the ARB price while you read the governance forum.

sections.heading: ETH on the L2 you leave, ETH on the L2 you enter
sections.body: Approve 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 with Arbitrum ETH. Move the USDC later with Base ETH. Neither gas balance is the output. The sentinel is not what you receive. A wallet with only ARB cannot start, and a Base wallet with only USDC cannot continue.

sections.heading: Wrong if ARB itself is the delivery
sections.body: This page is a sale. It is wrong for native ETH, wrong for the WETH predeploy, wrong for USDbC, and wrong on Nova. It is wrong if you wanted Circle USDC to remain the Arbitrum contract 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. That token is not the receive. Before you sign, compare 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 with 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on their explorers and stop if either address on the quote differs. Keep the source fee token in the wallet after you choose the trade size. Sign only on the source chain id named in this article, with the wallet network checked.

faqs.question: Will I receive ARB on Base?
faqs.answer: No. You sell 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One. The credit can be Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. Check Basescan. It is not USDbC. Voting power on the sold amount ends. Keep the ARB you still need before you sign. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Is this USDC native or bridged?
faqs.answer: Native Circle USDC, six decimals, at the address above, on chain id 8453. USDbC is the older bridged token and is not the output. If your app has not migrated, do not use this route for that app. Base is an L2. About 2 seconds is a block interval, not proof the app will recognize the token.

faqs.question: What pays gas for the ARB approval?
faqs.answer: Native ETH on Arbitrum One, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, chain id 42161. ARB cannot pay it. Base ETH cannot pay it. Nova is the wrong chain. You will also want ETH on Base later, because USDC does not pay fees on chain id 8453. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to ETH on Base. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and native ETH arrives here on Base.

The governance token 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is what you sell. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Hold separate ETH for the fee. Receive native ETH on Base, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, chain id 8453. Basescan shows the balance. It is not the WETH predeploy and not mainnet ETH. Base is an L2. Blocks are about 2 seconds. The route does not promise that pace.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for native ETH on Base. Base is L2 chain id 8453. Output is gas, not the WETH predeploy. Check Basescan. Leave source gas ready.

sections.heading: A governance sale that refills Base gas
sections.body: Pick this route when Base cannot sign and you are willing to sell ARB. The output can pay chain id 8453. It cannot pay chain id 42161, so the source ETH has to be there first. It is not 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. If a contract wanted that predeploy, you would still wrap, and the wrap would spend a slice of the ETH you just received.

sections.heading: Not one shared ETH across rollups
sections.body: Arbitrum ETH, Base ETH, and Ethereum ETH are three balances. This quote spends ARB, uses a little Arbitrum ETH as gas, and can credit Base ETH. Etherscan stays quiet. Basescan is the destination explorer. [Base](/chains/base) is chain id 8453. If the wallet is pointed at mainnet, you will not see the credit no matter how long you wait.

sections.heading: Price and voting weight
sections.body: The minimum ETH is a market number from a governance token. It expires. Unsold ARB keeps its vote. Sold ARB does not. Eighteen decimals on both assets do not mean one ARB becomes one ETH. Reread the floor on a fresh quote.

sections.heading: Wrong delivery if you needed ARB or a dollar
sections.body: Stop if ARB must remain ARB. Stop if you wanted Circle USDC or USDbC. Stop if you wanted the predeploy specifically and have no ETH to wrap. Stop on Nova. Stop if the balance you hold is WETH rather than the governance token. The spend address is the check.

faqs.question: Is the ETH I receive on Ethereum or on Base?
faqs.answer: On Base, chain id 8453, an L2. The marker is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Check Basescan, not Etherscan. You sell ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One. Mainnet ETH is chain id 1 and is not this credit. The WETH predeploy is not this credit either. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

faqs.question: Does selling ARB for Base ETH keep my vote?
faqs.answer: Only on ARB you do not sell. This page does not escrow tokens. The output is native ETH on Base, which has no ARB voting power. Lower the size if a proposal is close. Chain id 42161, not Nova, is where the remainder stays. About 2 seconds is a Base block, not a voting window.

faqs.question: Why is source ETH required to receive Base ETH?
faqs.answer: The signature is on Arbitrum One, which charges its own ETH. ARB cannot pay that fee. Base ETH arrives later and on another chain. Hold a source fee first. The sentinel means ETH on both rollups, but the balances are separate. Do not spend the source row down to zero.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to WETH on Base. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and Base WETH arrives here on Base.

Spend 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Confirm it on Arbiscan. Chain id 42161, not Nova. Gas is native ETH. Receive 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base. Basescan should show the predeploy, not the gas sentinel and not Ethereum WETH. Chain id 8453 is an L2. Blocks are about 2 seconds. That interval does not lock the ARB price.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for Base WETH at 0x4200. The predeploy is not gas and not mainnet WETH. Confirm it on Basescan. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: Three wrapped stories, one output
sections.body: You do not sell Arbitrum WETH. You do not receive Ethereum WETH. You can receive the Base predeploy. Those three addresses are 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Only the last one is the credit, and only on chain id 8453. The same predeploy hex on another OP-stack chain is not your wallet.

sections.heading: WETH on Base still needs ETH on Base
sections.body: The predeploy cannot pay gas. If you are funding a pool that pulls WETH, this output matches the call. If you are funding a wallet that needs to sign anything, you still need the sentinel balance. This route does not include it. Selling ARB also removes voting weight. The minimum WETH is a cross rate, not a governance wrap.

sections.heading: Allowance names the governance token
sections.body: If an approval appears, it should name 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 and it should be paid in ETH on Arbitrum One. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) puts that permission on the source. A screen that shows WETH as the spend means you switched routes. Go back before you grant allowance.

sections.heading: Wrong when gas or ARB is the thing you need
sections.body: Native ETH on Base is a different page. Circle USDC is a different page. Keeping ARB is not this page at all. Nova is the wrong source. Mainnet is the wrong destination. A local wrap of Base ETH does not involve the ARB contract on Arbiscan. Before you sign, compare 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 with 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on their explorers and stop if either address on the quote differs. If the quote expires, request another and read the new minimum before you sign. The destination fee token is a different balance from the one this route can credit.

faqs.question: Is 0x4200 Ethereum WETH?
faqs.answer: No. It is the WETH predeploy on Base, chain id 8453. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Confirm the credit on Basescan. You spend ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Native ETH, the sentinel, is not the output and is what Base uses for gas. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Can I move this WETH if I have no Base ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Chain id 8453 charges native ETH. The predeploy is an ERC-20. This route does not deliver the gas coin. About 2 seconds is a block interval, not a fee. You also need ETH on Arbitrum One to approve ARB. The two ETH balances are not interchangeable.

faqs.question: Does the ARB I sell become voting power on Base?
faqs.answer: No. Sold tokens leave Arbitrum One. They are not bridged as ARB, and WETH has no ARB vote. Keep the amount you need for governance. Chain id 42161, not Nova, holds whatever remains. If the quote expires, the WETH minimum expires with it. Confirm the address on the explorer before you sign.

intro:
Swap USDC from Arbitrum One to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. Circle USDC leaves Arbitrum One and Avalanche USDT arrives on C-Chain.

Spend Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, six decimals. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Gas in ETH. Receive 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Avalanche C-Chain. Snowtrace is the explorer. That USDT is Tether on C-Chain, chain id 43114, not the X-Chain and not the P-Chain. Gas there is AVAX. Blocks are about 2 seconds. That interval is not a bridge schedule.
description: Swap Circle USDC on Arbitrum One for Tether USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. C-Chain only, chain id 43114. Confirm the contract on Snowtrace. Read the quote again.

sections.heading: C-Chain, not the X-Chain address format
sections.body: Avalanche has more than one chain. This route's destination is the C-Chain, the EVM chain id 43114. An X-Chain address will not hold this USDT. A P-Chain address will not either. Snowtrace is the explorer that matches the contract 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. If your wallet is pointed at a subnet, you are also off the chain this quote credits.

sections.heading: Circle dollars become Tether
sections.body: The issuer changes. Both contracts are six decimals, so the amount should be read in whole tokens and still may not be one-for-one. Native Circle USDC on Avalanche is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, and this page does not deliver it. USDC.e, the older bridged dollar, is a third contract. If you needed Circle to remain Circle, switch routes before you approve.

Hold AVAX on chain id 43114 before you rely on moving 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

intro:
Swap WETH from Arbitrum One to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. Arbitrum WETH leaves the wallet and C-Chain USDT arrives here.

The spend is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Fee in ETH. The receive is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7, Tether, six decimals. Snowtrace is the check. It is not Circle USDC. C-Chain chain id 43114, not X-Chain. AVAX pays gas. Blocks about every 2 seconds. That pace is not the route's promise.
description: Swap Arbitrum WETH for C-Chain USDT at 0x970223. Tether, not Circle, C-Chain only. Confirm the contract on Snowtrace before you sign. Leave source gas ready.

sections.heading: One USDT address, not three
sections.body: Arbitrum Tether, Ethereum Tether, and 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 are different deployments. Only the last can be this credit, and only on chain id 43114. Six decimals make it look familiar. The chain id does not. A deposit page for ERC-20 USDT on Ethereum will not credit C-Chain USDT. Read Snowtrace and the deposit chain together.

sections.heading: C-Chain USDT still needs an Arbitrum WETH allowance
sections.body: The permission names 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. The sentinel is gas, not inventory. Unwrapping all WETH to pay gas removes the balance this page sells. Leave both. Nova will not match Arbiscan's contract for One.

sections.heading: Then the C-Chain wants AVAX
sections.body: USDT cannot pay fees. The sentinel output would have been AVAX, and this page did not select it. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) does not add a gas coin you left out of the quote. The minimum USDT is a price against wrapped ether. Refresh it.

sections.heading: Wrong ticker on either side
sections.body: Native ETH is the wrong input. Circle USDC and USDC.e are the wrong outputs. WAVAX and native AVAX are the wrong outputs if you wanted dollars. The X-Chain is the wrong destination. This page sells Arbitrum WETH for C-Chain Tether only. Before you sign, compare 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 with 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on their explorers and stop if either address on the quote differs. Do not treat a block interval on either chain as a promise for when the credit appears. The destination fee token is a different balance from the one this route can credit.

faqs.question: Which USDT contract is on the C-Chain for this route?
faqs.answer: 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7, six decimals. Check Snowtrace, chain id 43114. You spend WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Circle USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E is not the credit. The X-Chain will not list this ERC-20. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Why keep ETH if WETH is what I sell?
faqs.answer: Arbitrum One charges native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, chain id 42161. WETH cannot pay it. AVAX cannot pay it before it exists, and this route does not even deliver AVAX. About 2 seconds is a C-Chain block, not a fee waiver. Nova is the wrong source.

faqs.question: Is the output WAVAX because I started with WETH?
faqs.answer: No. Starting with wrapped ether does not preserve a wrapped ticker. WAVAX is not the receive contract. The receive is Tether. If you wanted native AVAX, open the route that uses the sentinel on the C-Chain. Read the quote's output address before you approve WETH.

intro:
Swap WETH from Arbitrum One to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. Arbitrum WETH leaves and native AVAX arrives here on C-Chain.

Sell 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Keep ETH for the fee. Receive native AVAX, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on chain id 43114. Snowtrace shows a balance, not WAVAX and not the X-Chain. Blocks are about 2 seconds. Unwrapping WETH on Arbitrum does not create this AVAX.
description: Swap Arbitrum WETH for native AVAX on the C-Chain. AVAX is gas, not WAVAX and not the X-Chain. Check 0x82aF on Arbiscan. Confirm the destination wallet.

sections.heading: Wrapped ether in, C-Chain gas out
sections.body: Use this when you hold WETH on Arbitrum One and need AVAX to operate on chain id 43114. You do not receive WAVAX. You do not receive a stablecoin. The output can pay C-Chain fees once it arrives. It cannot pay the Arbitrum approval. Leave native ETH beside the WETH so 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 can move.

sections.heading: Do not aim at the X-Chain
sections.body: Native AVAX exists on more than one Avalanche chain. This credit is C-Chain only. An X-Chain deposit address is the wrong string. P-Chain is wrong. Snowtrace for the C-Chain account balance is the check, not a token page at the sentinel. [Avalanche](/chains/avalanche) in this route means chain id 43114.

sections.heading: Not a one-for-one unwrap
sections.body: Withdraw on Arbitrum WETH returns ETH on chain id 42161. This quote is a market into AVAX. The minimum expires. Eighteen decimals do not make the amounts equal. If you unwrap first, you must switch to the native ETH route and reserve a fee. You cannot keep this page's input after the unwrap.

sections.heading: Wrong if the ETH peg should remain
sections.body: Stop if you need WAVAX. Stop if you need USDC or USDT. Stop if you hold native ETH rather than WETH. Stop for Nova. Stop if you thought the sentinel on Arbitrum already meant AVAX. It means ETH there. Before you sign, compare 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 with 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on their explorers and stop if either address on the quote differs. Keep the source fee token in the wallet after you choose the trade size. Sign only on the source chain id named in this article, with the wallet network checked.

faqs.question: Does this deliver WAVAX?
faqs.answer: No. The output is native AVAX, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on C-Chain chain id 43114. WAVAX is a different contract. You spend WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Snowtrace shows AVAX as a balance. The X-Chain is not the destination. About 2 seconds is a block interval, not a wrap.

faqs.question: Why is ETH still required?
faqs.answer: Gas on Arbitrum One is native ETH, not WETH. The approval and the swap need it on chain id 42161. AVAX arrives later and only on the C-Chain. It cannot fund the signature. If the ETH row is empty, WETH cannot move. Nova is not a spare gas chain.

faqs.question: Will a local unwrap put AVAX in my wallet?
faqs.answer: No. Unwrapping 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 pays ETH on Arbitrum One. This page is what can credit C-Chain AVAX. After an unwrap, use the native ETH input and keep a fee. Do not send the result to an X-Chain address. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to USDC on Avalanche C-Chain. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and Circle USDC arrives on C-Chain.

Sell 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. ARB is not gas. Hold ETH. Receive Circle USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, six decimals. Snowtrace should show it, not USDC.e and not ARB. C-Chain chain id 43114, not the X-Chain. AVAX pays later fees. Blocks about 2 seconds. That is not a sale schedule.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for Circle USDC on Avalanche C-Chain. Output is 0xB97E, not ARB and not USDC.e. Confirm it on Snowtrace. Read the quote again.

sections.heading: Governance sold, native USDC bought
sections.body: ARB you spend cannot vote, and it does not appear on Snowtrace as ARB. The dollar is Circle's native C-Chain contract. USDC.e is the bridged token this page skips. If a pool still calls the bridged contract USDC, your new balance will not connect. Check the pool before you give up voting weight.

sections.heading: No peg between ARB and the dollar
sections.body: The minimum USDC expires with the quote. Eighteen-decimal ARB against six-decimal USDC should be read as whole tokens only. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) will not lock the price. Refresh if you pause to compare Arbiscan with Snowtrace.

sections.heading: ETH, then AVAX
sections.body: Approve the governance token with ETH on chain id 42161. Move USDC with AVAX on chain id 43114. Neither gas coin is the output. An X-Chain address cannot hold the USDC even if you have AVAX there in another form.

sections.heading: Wrong if ARB is what must arrive
sections.body: Stop if you are relocating the governance token. Stop for USDT, AVAX, or WAVAX. Stop for USDC.e. Stop for the X-Chain and Nova. Stop if you wanted Arbitrum's own Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 as the receive. Before you sign, compare 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 with 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on their explorers and stop if either address on the quote differs. A stale minimum is a reason to ask for a fresh quote rather than signing the old one. Gas on the source chain is separate from the asset you hope to receive.

faqs.question: Will ARB show up on Snowtrace?
faqs.answer: Not from this route. You sell 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One. Snowtrace should be checked for Circle USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. That is not USDC.e. Voting power on the sold amount ends. The chain is the C-Chain, id 43114, not the X-Chain. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Is this USDC.e?
faqs.answer: No. Native Circle USDC uses 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, six decimals. The bridged token is a different address. If your app has not migrated, this page is the wrong dollar. About 2 seconds is a C-Chain block, not a sign that the app updated. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: What pays the ARB approval?
faqs.answer: Native ETH on Arbitrum One, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, chain id 42161. ARB cannot pay it. AVAX cannot pay it. You will want AVAX later on the C-Chain, because USDC does not pay fees there. Nova is the wrong source chain. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. ARB leaves the wallet Arbitrum One and C-Chain USDT arrives.

Governance token 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is the spend. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Gas is ETH. Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 is the receive, six decimals. Snowtrace confirms it. Not Circle, not ARB. C-Chain chain id 43114 only. AVAX is gas. Blocks about 2 seconds. Do not read that as a deadline.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for C-Chain USDT at 0x970223. You receive Tether, not ARB. C-Chain only. Check Snowtrace before you sign. Confirm the chain id.

sections.heading: Tether on the C-Chain, spelled as an address
sections.body: 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 is the contract to match. It is not Ethereum USDT and not Arbitrum USDT. A custodian that wants ERC-20 USDT on Ethereum will not credit this balance. The deposit chain has to say Avalanche C-Chain, and the contract has to match Snowtrace. X-Chain deposit strings are a different product.

sections.heading: The vote ends on the amount you sell
sections.body: This page does not bridge ARB as ARB. Unsold tokens can still vote from chain id 42161. Sold tokens are a USDT quote. The minimum moves with ARB's price. Eighteen versus six decimals. Read whole tokens, then sign only if the floor is acceptable.

sections.heading: Two fees around a governance sale
sections.body: ETH to approve 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. AVAX to move USDT later. [Avalanche](/chains/avalanche) is the C-Chain you are funding, not a general Avalanche address. If the approval screen shows WETH, you have left this route.

sections.heading: Wrong outputs for other goals
sections.body: Circle USDC, USDC.e, native AVAX, and WAVAX are different pages. Keeping ARB is not a page you reach by selling it. Nova and the X-Chain are the wrong networks. Check the spend address before allowance. Before you sign, compare 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 with 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on their explorers and stop if either address on the quote differs. If the quote expires, request another and read the new minimum before you sign. The destination fee token is a different balance from the one this route can credit. Check both explorers.

faqs.question: Does ARB arrive on the C-Chain?
faqs.answer: No. You sell 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One. The credit can be Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Check Snowtrace, chain id 43114. Voting weight on the sold tokens is gone. The X-Chain will not show this USDT. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Is this USDT six decimals?
faqs.answer: Yes. Read whole tokens on the quote anyway, because ARB uses eighteen. The contract is not Ethereum's Tether. You need ETH on chain id 42161 to sell, and AVAX on the C-Chain to move the result. About 2 seconds is a block interval, not a unit conversion.

faqs.question: Can ARB pay either fee?
faqs.answer: No. Source gas is native ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Destination gas is AVAX, which this route does not deliver. USDT cannot substitute. Nova is not chain id 42161. Fund ETH before you approve the governance token. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

intro:
Swap ARB from Arbitrum One to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. ARB leaves Arbitrum One and native AVAX arrives on C-Chain.

Spend 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. ARB does not pay gas. Hold ETH. Receive native AVAX, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, on chain id 43114. Snowtrace shows the balance. Not WAVAX. Not the X-Chain. Blocks are about 2 seconds. No promised arrival sits inside that interval.
description: Swap ARB on Arbitrum One for native AVAX on the C-Chain. AVAX is gas, chain id 43114, not WAVAX and not the X-Chain. Confirm both addresses on the explorers.

sections.heading: Sell voting weight for C-Chain gas
sections.body: This pair fits an Arbitrum wallet that holds ARB and a C-Chain wallet that cannot sign. The output can pay chain id 43114 fees. It cannot pay the Arbitrum fee, so ETH has to be there first. It is not WAVAX. If a contract wanted the wrapped token, you would wrap after arrival and spend a little of the AVAX to do it.

sections.heading: C-Chain address, not an X-Chain string
sections.body: AVAX as a word exists on several Avalanche chains. This credit is only the C-Chain gas balance. Paste a C-Chain account. Snowtrace will not show a token supply at the sentinel. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) does not retarget an X-Chain deposit address. P-Chain is wrong too.

sections.heading: A float into a float
sections.body: ARB and AVAX both move. The minimum expires. Unsold ARB keeps its vote. Sold ARB does not become a vote on Avalanche. Eighteen decimals do not imply one-for-one. Reread the floor on a fresh quote.

sections.heading: Wrong job if ARB must survive
sections.body: Stop if you are trying to relocate the governance token. Stop for USDC, USDT, or WAVAX. Stop for Nova. Stop if the coins you hold are WETH or native ETH. Stop if you meant a same-chain sale of ARB on Arbitrum One, which never touches Snowtrace. Before you sign, compare 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 with 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on their explorers and stop if either address on the quote differs. Do not treat a block interval on either chain as a promise for when the credit appears. Sign only on the source chain id named in this article, with the wallet network checked.

faqs.question: Is the AVAX native or WAVAX?
faqs.answer: Native. The marker is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on C-Chain chain id 43114. WAVAX is not the credit. You spend ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Snowtrace shows a balance, not a token page at the sentinel. The X-Chain is a different destination. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Do I keep ARB voting power?
faqs.answer: Only on the amount you do not sell. This route does not escrow ARB and does not mint it on Avalanche. The credit is AVAX. Lower the size if a proposal needs you. Remainder stays on chain id 42161, not Nova. About 2 seconds is a C-Chain block, not a voting extension.

faqs.question: What gas is required before AVAX arrives?
faqs.answer: Native ETH on Arbitrum One. ARB cannot pay it. The AVAX you are trying to receive cannot pay it either. The sentinel on chain id 42161 is ETH. Fund that row first. Then use the C-Chain AVAX for later transactions. Do not send the credit to an X-Chain address.

intro:
Swap USDC from Arbitrum One to USDT on Solana. Circle USDC leaves Arbitrum One and SPL USDT arrives on Solana.

Spend Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, an ERC-20. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Gas is ETH, and you may approve that contract. Receive the SPL mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Solscan is the explorer. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana. The receive wallet is a Solana address in Phantom, not a 0x account. Slots are near 400 milliseconds. That speed is not a bridge schedule.
description: Swap Circle USDC on Arbitrum One for SPL USDT on Solana. Mint Es9vMF on Solscan. Use Phantom, not an Ethereum address. No ERC-20 approval on Solana now.

sections.heading: The receive side is an SPL mint
sections.body: Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB is Tether's USDT on Solana. It is not Arbitrum Tether and not Ethereum Tether. Solscan is where you read the mint. Phantom, or another Solana wallet, must be the destination. Pasting your Arbitrum 0x address into the receive field will not create a Solana token account. There is nothing for an ERC-20 approve call to do on that side.

sections.heading: Issuer changes with the runtime
sections.body: Circle USDC leaves. Tether's SPL mint can arrive. Both target a dollar and the quote can still gap. Read the minimum. Native Circle USDC on Solana is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, and this page does not deliver that mint. If a Solana app wants Circle, this Tether balance will not satisfy it.

sections.heading: ETH starts the hop, SOL spends later
sections.body: Arbitrum One still charges ETH, and USDC.e will not fund the spend. After USDT exists in Phantom, further Solana transactions need a little native SOL for fees. This route's output is the USDT mint, not the wrapped SOL mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the hop. It does not turn Solana into an EVM chain.

sections.heading: Wrong wallet, wrong mint, wrong dollar
sections.body: Stop if the destination is an exchange EVM deposit. Stop if you need Circle's Solana USDC. Stop if you need SOL for gas and have none. Stop on Nova. Stop if you expected an ERC-20 approval popup on the Solana side. That popup belongs only to the Arbitrum USDC, if allowance is missing.

faqs.question: Can I receive this USDT at my Ethereum address?
faqs.answer: No. Solana uses a different address format. The mint is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, checked on Solscan. Phantom, not an EVM wallet, should be the destination. You spend Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbitrum One. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Is Solana USDT the same as Circle USDC?
faqs.answer: No. Circle's Solana USDC mint is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. This route can credit Tether's mint instead. The issuer changes. Read the minimum. A slot near 400 milliseconds is a Solana timing fact, not a promise that the SPL balance is already visible. Confirm that address on the explorer before you sign, and refresh the quote if it has expired.

faqs.question: Do I approve USDT on Solana?
faqs.answer: No. SPL transfers do not use the ERC-20 approve pattern. Any approval you sign is for Circle USDC on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, paid in ETH. You will still want a little native SOL in Phantom later, because this output is not the wrapped SOL mint and will not pay Solana fees by itself.

intro:
Swap USDC from Arbitrum One to SOL on Solana. Circle USDC leaves Arbitrum One and wrapped SOL is the mint that can arrive.

Spend 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbitrum One. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Fee in ETH. The destination mint is So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, wrapped SOL, which you read on Solscan. It is an SPL mint, not native lamports by itself and not an ERC-20. Phantom holds it. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana. Slots near 400 milliseconds are not a bridge clock.
description: Swap Circle USDC on Arbitrum One for the wrapped SOL mint on Solana. Mint So111 on Solscan. Phantom only. Not an ERC-20 approval. Read the minimum first.

sections.heading: So111 is wrapped SOL, not a 0x token
sections.body: The quote names So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. Wallets often display that balance as SOL. It is still the wrapped mint, an SPL token account, not the system-account lamports that pay fees until it is unwrapped. If you needed only fee lamports and the quote delivers the wrapped mint, confirm whether your wallet unwraps automatically. Do not search Etherscan for this mint. Solscan is the explorer.

sections.heading: A Solana address, or nothing arrives
sections.body: Phantom, Solflare, and similar wallets use base58 addresses. Your Arbitrum address cannot be the recipient. There is no approval transaction on Solana for this mint. The approval, if it appears, is Circle USDC on chain id 42161. [Solana](/chains/solana) is the destination runtime. Nova is not a stand-in for the source, and an EVM network is not a stand-in for the destination.

sections.heading: Dollars into a volatile mint
sections.body: Circle USDC is six decimals and targets a dollar. SOL does not. The minimum on the wrapped mint expires with the quote. USDC.e on Arbitrum will not fund the spend. You need ETH on Arbitrum One to start. You may already need a little SOL in the destination wallet so it can pay rent or fees around the token account. This route is not a promise that an empty Phantom can do everything with zero SOL.

sections.heading: Wrong if you wanted USDT or an EVM gas coin
sections.body: Tether's SPL mint is a different output. Native ETH and BNB are meaningless on Solana. Stop if the receive field is a 0x address. Stop if you wanted Circle USDC to remain the Solana USDC mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Stop on Nova.

faqs.question: Is So111 native SOL or wrapped SOL?
faqs.answer: It is the wrapped SOL mint, So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. Solscan shows that mint. Wallets may label it SOL. Fee-paying lamports live on the system account until wrapped SOL is unwrapped. You spend Circle USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana. Use Phantom, not a 0x address.

faqs.question: Can I paste my Arbitrum address as the recipient?
faqs.answer: No. Solana addresses are not 0x strings. The destination wallet should be Phantom or a similar Solana wallet. Arbiscan is only for the USDC you sell on chain id 42161. A slot near 400 milliseconds does not mean an EVM address can hold SPL tokens.

faqs.question: Does this route include an approve call on Solana?
faqs.answer: No. SPL is not ERC-20. You might approve Circle USDC on Arbitrum One, and that approval is paid in ETH. You do not approve So111 on Solana. If the wallet offers an Ethereum-style approval for the destination, you are on the wrong network. USDC.e on Arbitrum is also the wrong spend.

intro:
Swap USDT from Arbitrum One to USDC on Solana. Tether USDT leaves Arbitrum One and Circle USDC arrives on Solana.

Sell Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. Gas in ETH. Receive Circle's SPL mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Solscan is the explorer. Phantom is the wallet. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana, and a 0x address cannot hold the mint. Slots near 400 milliseconds are not a delivery promise.
description: Swap Tether USDT on Arbitrum One for Circle USDC on Solana. Mint EPjFW on Solscan. Phantom address only. No ERC-20 approval on Solana. Read the minimum first.

sections.heading: Circle's Solana mint is not an EVM contract
sections.body: EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v is the USDC to expect in Phantom. It is not 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 and not Ethereum's 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Those are Circle too, on other runtimes. Solscan is the check. If you import an EVM address into a Solana field, nothing about this mint will line up.

sections.heading: Tether leaves, Circle arrives
sections.body: The issuer changes as the chain changes. Six-decimal habits on both sides still do not make a perfect one-for-one. Read the minimum. Tether's own Solana mint, Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, is what you would receive if you had wanted the ticker to stay USDT. This page does the opposite.

sections.heading: Source approval only

sections.heading: A governance sale into wrapped SOL
sections.body: People open this page when they hold ARB and need SOL in Phantom. The output is the wrapped mint, which wallets often label SOL. Native lamports are what pay fees, so you may unwrap after arrival. You do not receive an ARB mint. Voting weight leaves with the tokens you sell. sections.body: Phantom's address is the recipient. The Arbitrum address is only the signer on chain id 42161. Mixing them strands the intent before a route exists. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is useful background, and it still assumes you can tell an SPL mint from an ERC-20. So111 will not appear on Arbiscan.

sections.body: 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 may need allowance, paid in ETH. The minimum wrapped SOL expires when the quote expires. ARB and SOL both float. Do not treat equal-looking decimals as a one-for-one redeem. SOL uses nine decimals. ARB uses eighteen. Read the quote.

faqs.question: Why is ETH required to buy SOL?
faqs.answer: Because the signature is on Arbitrum One, and that chain charges ETH, sentinel 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. ARB cannot pay it. The SOL mint cannot pay it. A slot near 400 milliseconds is a Solana fact, not a waiver of the source fee. Fund ETH, then watch Phantom for So111.
